items.loc: Huawei Ohm Research Center (Nuremberg), Nürnberg, Germany
items.desc:
Huawei's Ohm Research Center (Nuremberg) is responsible for Advanced Technology Research, Architecture Evolution Design and Strategic Technology Planning. 
 Huawei Digital Power is a business unit within Huawei that provides Enterprise & Industry customers, products and solutions like clean power generation, transportation electrification, site power facilities, data center facilities, and embedded power. Huawei Digital Power is committed to integrate Digital and Power Electronics technologies to provide customers with high-quality, energy-efficient, green, and low-carbon power electronics products, facilitating their business success. 
 The Power Conversion Technology Laboratory within Huawei's Ohm Research Center (Nuremberg) is responsible for Advanced Digital Power Technology Research, Architecture Evolution Design and Strategic Technology Planning, and plays an important role in the Huawei Digital Power business in the design and development of power converters and control systems for applications such as PV Solar & Battery Energy Storage Field, Data Centers, Electric Vehicle, and Embedded Power Supply. 
 Join us as a
 PhD Student – Circuit Breakers for Renewable Energy Integration (m/f/d) 
 Your mission 
 Conduct literature reviews and technical analysis on medium-voltage circuit breakers (MV-CBs), focusing on renewable energy integration (e.g., solid-state/hybrid CB topologies, fault current limiting, and protection strategies) 
 Design and perform experiments to validate the performance of next-gen CBs (solid-state/hybrid), including drive unit optimization, dynamic response testing, and failure diagnostics 
 Perform multiphysics simulations (COMSOL, Siemens Simcenter) and CFD analysis to evaluate electro-thermal-mechanical behavior of CB geometries and optimize designs 
 Develop and test experimental circuits (e.g., gate drivers, snubber circuits, sensor interfaces) and functional modules in a lab environment 
 Publish research findings in high-impact journals and present at international conferences 
 Generate patents and technical reports to protect innovations and support commercialization 
 Maintain lab safety protocols, equipment logs, and calibration records in compliance with EHS standards 
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams (power electronics, materials, controls) for system-level validation and integration 
 Your areas of expertise 
 Master of Science (MSc) or equivalent degree in electrical engineering, power electronics, physics or related field 
 Hands‑on experience with PCB assembly (soldering, wiring) and basic lab equipment (multimeter, oscilloscope, current/voltage sensors) 
 Experience in working with current interruption experiments in MV/HV levels is preferred 
 Experience with discreet and modular power electronics components (e.g. MOSFET/IGBT device, gate driver) is desirable 
 Good working knowledge of one or more of the following software tools is advantageous: Python, PLECS, Modelica 
 Flexibility to learn new things and work in highly dynamic atmosphere 
 Excellent communication skills in English language; knowledge of German is an advantage

items.title: PhD Student - Privacy Enhancing Technologies for LLMs and AI Agents
items.loc: Huawei Heisenberg Research Center (Munich), München, Germany
items.desc:
Huawei's Munich Research Center is responsible for advanced technology research, architectural development, design and strategic engineering of our products.
 Artificial Intelligence agents are rapidly becoming part of everyday life; however, they also introduce significant privacy risks: sensitive information may be unintentionally memorized, exposed across agent interactions, or leaked through internal reasoning and decision processes. 
 Our research group focuses on the intersection of Privacy, Security, and Artificial Intelligence, with a particular emphasis on privacy risks in LLM-based and multi-agent systems. Our goal is to design novel privacy-enhancing technologies that make next-generation AI agents trustworthy, secure, and deployable in real-world applications. 
 We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate who is excited about cutting-edge research in AI and privacy, and who wants to contribute to shaping the future of trustworthy intelligent systems. 
 Join us as a
 PhD Student - Privacy Enhancing Technologies for LLMs and AI Agents (m/f/d) 
 Your Responsibilities 
 Conduct systematic research on privacy risks in AI agent systems, with a focus on components such as memory, reasoning, decision-making, and multi-agent communication. 
 Develop novel privacy-preserving methods to mitigate risks such as sensitive data leakage, prompt-based extraction, unintended memorization, and privacy violations during agent collaboration. 
 Explore and apply privacy frameworks to agent-based architectures. 
 Design, implement, and evaluate prototypes in realistic LLM- and multi-agent environments. 
 Publish your research in leading conferences and journals in machine learning, AI security, and privacy (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CCS, S&P, PETS). 
 Collaborate with academic and industrial partners to transfer research results into real-world systems and products. 
 Your Areas of Expertise 
 Master’s degree (or equivalent) in computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or a related field. 
 Strong theoretical and practical background in machine learning, deep learning, or natural language processing. 
 Proficient programming skills in Python and experience with at least one major deep learning framework (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX). 
 Familiarity with large language models and agent-based systems is a plus. 
 Knowledge of privacy and security techniques relevant to ML systems is a plus. 
 Prior research experience or publications in machine learning, security, or privacy venues is advantageous. 
 Excellent written and spoken English. 
 If you are enthusiastic to shape the German Research Center in Munich together with us, being part of a multicultural team and growing environment, feel free to contact us. Driving future technologies with focus on customer satisfaction is a one of our missions. Join us!

items.title: PhD Measuring and Scaling Agentic Software Engineering (f/m/x)
items.desc:
THE FUTURE IS WHAT WE CREATE WHEN WE TAKE OUR VISIONS TO THE LIMITS. 
 PHD AT THE BMW GROUP. 
 Bridging the gap between your doctoral studies and the kind of career challenge you’re looking for isn’t always easy. That’s why our ProMotion PhD programme gives you the opportunity to apply your passion and scientific expertise to very real challenges that could shape the future of mobility. If selected, you’ll have the chance to really develop your own future career path with us through your practice-related thesis, promote your chosen specialty from within – and position yourself to secure the career you’ve always wanted.
 Our New Technologies team explores and evaluates emerging technologies and brings the most promising ones into productive use across the BMW Group. Agentic software engineering is one of these technologies, and as a PhD candidate, you help find ways to systematically measure agentic software development and scale it to real-world use. 
 What awaits you? 
 You design benchmarks that evaluate coding agents on real automotive codebases across the full development lifecycle. 
 Within this project, you investigate where agents lose relevant code between exploration and generation - a failure mode that grows with codebase size and remains unmeasured. 
 Building on these insights, you explore methods that help agents preserve and use relevant code more effectively. 
 In this role, you help develop verification and testing approaches that keep agent-generated code trustworthy without slowing down development. 
 Together with the team, you benchmark agent configurations, LLMs, harnesses and scaffolding across heterogeneous stacks such as embedded C/C++, Java, Python and Go. 
 Finally, you translate your findings into research and deployment frameworks that can be applied at real-world scale. 
 What should you bring along? 
 Studies in computer science, data science, mathematics or a comparable field. 
 Solid knowledge of machine learning, in particular large language models and agentic systems. 
 Strong programming skills in Python; experience with C/C++, Java or Go is an advantage. 
 Hands-on experience with agent evaluation and benchmarking, for example SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, tau-bench or comparable frameworks. 
 Ideally first publications or submissions at relevant scientific venues during your studies. 
 Very good English language skills; German is an advantage. 
 Are you excited about advancing the science and practice of agentic software engineering at automotive scale? Apply now! 
 Note: Please apply exclusively online through our career portal. Applications submitted via other channels (including email) cannot be considered. Citizens of countries outside the European Union must have a valid residence or work permit for the duration of the program. 
 If you make it to the next round, you will receive an invitation to a video interview by e-mail. Please also check your spam folder regularly. 
 What do we offer? 
 Comprehensive mentoring & onboarding. 
 Personal & professional development. 
 Flexible working hours. 
 Digital offers & mobile working. 
 Attractive & fair remuneration. 
 Annual special payments such as vacation pay and Christmas bonus. 
 Apartment offers for students (subject to availability & only Munich). 
 And many other benefits – see bmw.jobs/benefits 
 Start date: from now on 
 Duration: 36 months 
 Working hours: Part-time 
 You can find helpful tips on your application and the application process here . 
 At the BMW Group, we place great importance on equal treatment and equal opportunities. Our recruiting decisions are based on the personality, experience, and skills of the applicants. Learn more here .

 Du unterstützt bei der Forschung an einem multimodalen, agentischen KI-System zur automatisierten Erkennung und strukturierten Beschreibung elektronischer Komponenten im Cost Engineering Elektronik. 
 Außerdem wirkst du mit bei der Analyse bestehender Cost-Engineering-Prozesse für Leiterplatten, Steuergeräte und elektronische Bauteile sowie bei der Ableitung fachlicher und technischer Anforderungen. 
 Darüber hinaus trägst du bei zum Aufbau und zur Aufbereitung heterogener Datengrundlagen, insbesondere PCB-Scans, geometrische Messdaten, Lieferantendokumentationen, Stücklisten, Datenblätter und externe Bauteildatenbanken. 
 Du unterstützt bei der Entwicklung textbasierter Verfahren zur Extraktion und Strukturierung von Bauteilparametern aus Datenblättern, Bill of Materials und weiteren technischen Dokumenten. 
 Du entwickelst bildbasierte Verfahren zur Erkennung, Segmentierung und Beschreibung elektronischer Komponenten auf Leiterplatten, einschließlich Package-Geometrie, Pin-Konfigurationen und Markierungen. 
 Außerdem unterstützt du bei der Konzeption und Umsetzung der Fusion von Text-, Bild- und Messdaten zur Reduktion mehrdeutiger Bauteilhypothesen sowie zur robusten Bauteilidentifikation inklusive Plausibilitätsprüfungen und Confidence Scoring. 
 Schließlich wirkst du mit bei der Validierung des Systems anhand gelabelter Datensätze, externer Datenquellen und Konsistenzchecks sowie bei der Entwicklung eines prototypischen Systems mit Anbindung an repräsentative Cost-Engineering-Workflows und Datenbanken. 
 Was bringst du mit? 
 Abgeschlossenes Studium mit Masterabschluss in Künstlicher Intelligenz, Informatik, Elektrotechnik, Ingenieurwissenschaften, Data Science, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder einem vergleichbaren Studiengang. 
 Fundierte Kenntnisse in Python sowie praktische Erfahrung mit Machine Learning, Deep Learning oder datengetriebener Modellierung. 
 Erfahrung oder starkes Interesse an Computer Vision, Vision-Language Models, Large Language Models, Transformer-Architekturen, PyTorch, HuggingFace oder vergleichbaren Frameworks. 
 Verständnis für strukturierte und unstrukturierte technische Daten, z.B. Datenblätter, Stücklisten, Messdaten, Tabellen und Datenbanken. 
 Interesse an elektronischen Komponenten, Leiterplatten, Steuergeräten und deren Bedeutung für Cost Engineering, Lieferantenbewertung und technische Optimierung. 
 Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. 
 Du möchtest an der Schnittstelle von Künstlicher Intelligenz, Elektronik, Cost Engineering und industrieller Anwendung promovieren? Bewirb dich jetzt!

items.desc: PhD fellowship in climate and health epidemiology A 3-year PhD fellowship is available at the Work, Environment and Cancer group at the Danish Cancer Institute. The position We are seeking a PhD student to work on a large EU-funded consortium project, Understanding and Preventing Climate-Related Health Risks through Mediating Pathways (U-PATH) . Europe is the fastest-warming continent, yet evidence that separates direct heat effects from effects mediated by other environmental exposures, such as air pollution, aeroallergens, noise, and indoor overheating, is still lacking. U-PATH brings together 15 international research institutions to investigate how climate exposures relate to cardiovascular and respiratory disease, with a particular focus on the mediating role of environmental exposures. The Work, Environment and Cancer group’s main tasks in U-PATH include: coordinating the harmonization of epidemiological data from cohorts in five countries contributing data and analyses from a Danish nationwide cohort conducting measurement campaigns of indoor summer temperatures, which will be used to develop a model for indoor heat exposure assessment coordinating analyses of associations between long-term residential indoor and outdoor heat events and risk of cardiovascular and respiratory disease across the cohorts The Work, Environment and Cancer research group is a dynamic multi-national team of researchers dedicated to studying the effects of environmental and occupational exposures on the development of cancer and other diseases. Your main responsibilities Conduct indoor temperature measurement campaigns Contribute to developing a model for indoor exposure assessment Link climate exposure data to Danish residential addresses Generate analysis-ready datasets with climate and environmental exposures, health outcomes, and potential confounders for the Danish population Analyze associations between climate and environmental exposures and risk of cardiovascular and respiratory disease, in collaboration with key U-PATH partners Write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals Present results at U-PATH consortium meetings and international conferences PhD enrolment You will be enrolled as a PhD student at a Danish university and supervised by researchers from the Work, Environment and Cancer group. Enrolment is subject to approval by the relevant PhD school, and it is a prerequisite for receiving the stipend that you are enrolled as a PhD student. Your progress as a PhD student will be assessed at regular intervals. As part of your PhD studies, you will be required, among other things, to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS and to undertake a research stay of 3-6 months at a foreign research institution. Qualifications Required A master’s degree (completed or nearly completed) in public health, epidemiology, statistics, or related discipline Experience in statistical programming, preferably in SAS and/or R A systematic and well-organized work approach, with strong planning and collaboration skills Excellent written and spoken English An advantage Experience with statistical analyses in quantitative epidemiological research Experience with large datasets and register-based data Experience with GIS software, such as QGIS Experience with contributing to peer-reviewed publications Interest in or experience with field data collection We offer An inspiring and dynamic working environment in an interdisciplinary research center (biologists, human biologists, public health scientists, medical doctors, data managers, psychologists, statisticians, etc.) where we work with many different epidemiological and biological topics. The research department regularly hosts interdisciplinary seminars with external lecturers on biological and epidemiological research areas and internal courses on relevant topics. Also, we have a Postdoc network that arranges regular meetings and seminars. Salary, pension, and conditions of employment will be in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement between the Danish government and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). We offer canteen, fruit scheme, sports- and art clubs as well as physiotherapy. You will initially be employed as research assistants to allow time for enrollment as PhD students at the University. You are expected to write your PhD application with support from your supervisor. The Danish Cancer Society of course has a no smoking policy during working hours. Start date: The position is a 3-year full-time position and is open from January 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. More information For specific information about the project or the position, please contact Group Leader and Professor Mette Sørensen, mettes@cancer.dk, +45 3525 7626 Application and deadline Submit your application no later than 15th of November 2026 . Applications submitted after this date will not be considered. We only accept applications through our electronic system at www.cancer.dk/job. The application must include: A cover letter (maximum two pages) describing how your qualifications match the project A detailed CV A Master's degree diploma, or documentation of expected completion A list of publications, if any, including submitted manuscripts Application due 11/15/2026 Start date 1/1/2027 Work hours Position category Position type Workplace Copenhagen Homepage https://www.cancer.dk Contact Mette Sørensen Gruppeleder 35257626 More vacant positions Follow us

items.title: PHD POSITION IN URBAN SOCIAL RESILIENCE WITHIN SUSTAINABILITY AND PLANNING
items.desc: Description of the Position Aalborg University invites applications for a PhD position in Sustainability and Planning Research focusing on urban resilience from a systemic and planning-oriented perspective. The PhD project explores the dynamic relationships between people, places, and material environments and is situated within an emerging research agenda investigating how design thinking and planning practices can support circularity and sustainability initiatives in cities. This PhD position, funded by the project “Co-creating regenerative green-social infrastructures for urban circular economies” ( WeGrowCircle ) through the Driving Urban Transitions Partnership, is part of a new interdisciplinary thematic research initiative addressing Urban Social Resilience (USR) with particular attention to care ethics, participatory processes, and social innovation as guiding perspectives. The successful candidate will contribute to interdisciplinary research activities, empirical studies, and scholarly publications in close collaboration with other members of the USR initiative across the Department of Sustainability & Planning and the Department of Architecture, Design & Media Technology. The position further offers engagement in a wider research network spanning urban sustainability, innovation, planning, design, and architecture. The position is available from 1 January 2027 or soon hereafter, and with employment in the Sustainability, Innovation and Policy research group. The duration of the position is three years. Research Focus The PhD project addresses the pressing challenge of developing urban social resilience in cities, with a particular focus on how social actors, relations, and practices can gain agency in resilience-building processes through inclusive, collaborative, participatory, and planning-based approaches across actors, organisations, and institutions. The project is grounded in a socio-material planning and design perspective, where urban resilience is understood as an emergent quality produced through interactions between social dynamics, institutional frameworks, and material and spatial configurations. Within this framework, the PhD project must in particular contribute to: establishing a shared conceptual and methodological foundation for the WeGrowCircle project, e.g. as a Resilient Urban Commons Framework mapping and analysing actor landscapes, relations, and key dynamics in the development of urban social resilience and regenerative green-social infrastructures (GSIs) developing and testing an inclusive co-creation process for GSI design, exploring stewardship and governance models for resilient and collective land management, evaluating how GSIs can improve biodiversity, circular practices, sufficiency, and social well-being; and generating evidence and recommendations for integrating GSIs into local planning, climate action and community practice. The PhD project may adopt different disciplinary perspectives, empirical focus areas, and methodological approaches within the broader field of urban social resilience and planning. At the same time, it is expected that the project will relate to and further develop the research environment’s work with socio-material approaches, participatory and interactive planning, as well as co-design and co-production in the context of urban resilience. Applicants are therefore expected to develop and outline a preliminary research proposal (1–3 pages) that presents their initial considerations regarding research focus, research design, and methodological approach in relation to urban social resilience within a planning and design perspective. Research Context The specific empirical context of the PhD project is closely linked to the WeGrowCircle project and thus mainly to the Aalborg Living Lab. However, engagement with one or more of the other three living labs (Brussels, Gothenburg, Bucharest) in the project is expected. Decision about which one(s) is intentionally left open at this point, and need not be considered in the application. Your Competences Applicants should demonstrate a strong interest in exploring how urban resilience is shaped through the interplay between social and material dimensions. The PhD project is expected to investigate planning and design processes with particular attention to participatory, co-design, and co-production approaches, as well as the use of mapping as an analytical and generative research method. Applicants must hold a Master’s degree in sustainability and planning, urban studies, sustainability and design, geography, or a related discipline. Experience with qualitative, participatory, and design-oriented research methods—including co-design or co-production—is considered a significant advantage. The ideal candidate is motivated to work in interdisciplinary research environments and is interested in collaborating across disciplines and with a wide range of urban stakeholders, including planners, designers, and public sector actors. The candidate should demonstrate curiosity, independence, and initiative, and be motivated to develop and conduct a PhD project involving co-design and co-production in close collaboration with supervisors and research partners. Qualification requirements PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution. What we Offer The position offers a dynamic and interdisciplinary research environment rooted in contemporary sustainability and planning research. The PhD candidate will have the opportunity to contribute to and shape a growing body of research on design and planning for urban social resilience. The position includes support for scholarly publications and public communication of research, and carries an obligation for teaching, supervising, and involvement in the Department’s bachelor and master programmes on planning and sustainability. How to apply Your application must include the following: Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position Curriculum Vitae (CV) Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) A preliminary research proposal (1–3 pages) Other relevant documents The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. Do you have any questions? You may obtain further information from Associate Professor Martin Lehmann martinl@plan.aau.dk concerning the scientific aspects of the stipend. For further information about stipends and salary as well as practical issues concerning the application procedure contact Lisbeth Diinhoff, The Doctoral School at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design, email: ld@adm.aau.dk Further information Read more about our recruitment process here. The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts. Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not. The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. Read more about The Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design Salary and terms of employment The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”. There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position. Aalborg University - Knowledge for the worldAalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen. items.title: THESE EN INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE (H/F)
items.desc: 35170 Bruz, Bretagne CDD A propos de Sogitec Venez faire décoller vos talents à nos côtés ! Société d’ingénierie en aéronautique, SOGITEC est leader dans la conception, le développement, la production et la fourniture de produits et services de simulation, pour la formation et l’entrainement au sol des pilotes et mécaniciens qui emploient et soutiennent les aéronefs réels. Filiale à 100% de Dassault Aviation, l’entreprise compte plus de 300 collaborateurs et s’impose comme un partenaire de premier niveau au service des constructeurs aéronautiques. Combinant sa longue expérience des exigences opérationnelles et ses compétences dans l’intégration des nouvelles technologies, telles que l’intelligence artificielle ou la réalité virtuelle, SOGITEC investit dans la recherche et l’innovation. Ainsi, SOGITEC intervient en tant que maître d'œuvre de programmes français et internationaux, complexes, pluriannuels et impliquant de multiples coopérations industrielles. SOGITEC s’appuie sur un socle d’affaires en forte consolidation grâce aux ventes du RAFALE et de ses moyens de simulation, dont il est le fournisseur exclusif. De plus, SOGITEC s’adapte aux besoins d’entraînement des Forces aériennes pour les derniers hélicoptères d’AIRBUS Helicopter par la fourniture des simulateurs de NH90 et prochainement du tout nouveau HIL (H160M). Enfin, SOGITEC développe de nouveaux produits de simulation dans les domaines des drones et des hélicoptères, y compris pour le personnel dédié à l’emploi du treuil et de l’armement. Ces succès reposent sur des équipes passionnées et dynamiques, d’un très haut niveau d’expertise technique, sur l’envie de repousser les limites et la capacité à faire face aux exigences d’une activité en constante évolution pour construire l’avenir. Votre mission THESE EN INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE : CONTRÔLE PAR INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE DES ENTITÉS VIRTUELLES D’UN SIMULATEUR DE VOL AFIN D’ATTEINDRE LES OBJECTIFS DE LEUR MISSION. A SOGITEC, VOUS SEREZ : Dans le cadre de ses activités de simulation d’avions d’armes et d’hélicoptères, SOGITEC souhaite renforcer sa capacité à modéliser et à simuler le comportement des forces en présence à partir de techniques d’intelligence artificielle. Les simulateurs développés par ses équipes s’appuient sur un serveur tactique pour animer les entités aériennes, terrestres et navales présentes sur le théâtre d’opérations virtuel. Pour un opérateur ou un moniteur simulation, paramétrer chacune de ces entités requiert un travail fastidieux pour obtenir le résultat souhaité en termes de déplacement ou réaction. Depuis plusieurs années, SOGITEC investigue des méthodes d’apprentissage machine afin d’envisager un contrôle plus intuitif des entités programmables. Les algorithmes employés ont jusqu’ici produit des résultats prometteurs mais l’entreprise souhaite poursuivre ses travaux de recherche afin d’identifier des solutions flexibles capables de gérer des situations plus complexes (grand nombre d’entités, diversité des missions/situations, etc). Dans ce contexte SOGITEC et ISAE-SUPAERO souhaitent travailler en collaboration, au travers d’une thèse CIFRE, pour lever les verrous technologiques correspondants :  Recenser les missions d’intérêt, identifier le meilleur moyen de modéliser ces missions et de les paramétrer par un utilisateur.  Identifier l’architecture algorithmique de contrôle des entités qui doit en résulter.  Statuer sur le niveau de contrôle.  Évaluer la scalabilité/portabilité de la solution. Votre profil AUJOURD’HUI VOUS ÊTES : Vous devez disposer d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+5 avec un M2 recherche ou avec une expérience avérée de recherche (obligatoire). Cadre de travail : Vous serez rattaché(e) à la Direction des Simulations à SOGITEC, et serez sous la responsabilité de son chef de service. En tant que doctorant(e) spécialisé(e) dans l’IA, vous devez être en capacité d’imaginer de nouvelles solutions dans ce domaine, adaptées à nos problématiques. Vous serez également inscrit(e) à l’ISAE-SUPAERO, Université de Toulouse, qui sera votre laboratoire d’accueil doctoral. Vous serez rattaché(e) au département DCAS, sous la supervision de ses directeurs de thèse. Vous participerez également à des projets stratégiques intégrant (non exhaustif) le Deep Learning avancé, Apprentissage par Renforcement (RL) ou encore l’IA générative et modèles de langage (LLM), et serez en en étroite collaboration avec les équipes techniques et métiers afin de transformer les besoins fonctionnels en solutions algorithmiques performantes et industrialisables chez SOGITEC. Dans ce cadre, vous réaliserez des travaux d'études bibliographiques, d'études algorithmiques, de prototypage, de développement logiciel, de spécification logicielle, d'architecture et conception, de test des solutions (robustesse, performance, etc), de rédaction de publications (et participation à des conférences du domaine). Compétences scientifiques et techniques recherchées : Fondamentaux scientifiques (mathématique, statistique, probabilité, algèbre, optimisation numérique…) et techniques de développement logiciel (langages programmation C++, Python, algorithmie en général…) solides Deep Learning, réseaux de neurones, méthodes d’entrainement… Planification sous incertitude, Décision Séquentielle, Apprentissage par renforcement... IA Générative & LLM (Transformers, Prompt engineering, RAG, Fine-tuning, Agentique…) Industrialisation & MLOps (Hardware et Infrastructure, CI/CD, déploiement des modèles en production, Monitoring). Compétences relationnelles et non techniques recherchées : De curiosité scientifique et technique, pour le secteur défense en particulier. D’adaptation (au domaine de l’aéronautique et la simulation de vol, à la complexité du sujet, à la diversité des compétences requises). D’appétences pour les défis technologiques. De capacités d’abstraction du problème posé. De prise de recul et d’anticipation. D’autonomie et de proposition d’idées. D’aisance organisationnelle et relationnelle.

items.title: PhD Position in EU Doctoral Network "PANDORA"
items.desc: PhD Position in EU Doctoral Network "PANDORA" Réf ABG-140512 Sujet de Thèse 13/10/2026 Financement de l'Union européenne Sorbonne Université Lieu de travail Paris - Ile-de-France - France Intitulé du sujet PhD Position in EU Doctoral Network "PANDORA" Champs scientifiques Biologie Santé, médecine humaine, vétérinaire Mots clés Biological sciences, Biology, Medical sciences, Neurosciences, Immunology Description du sujet The position focuses on "Evaluating how complement dysregulation influences mononuclear phagocyte accumulation in AMD" within the MSCA Doctoral Network PANDORA (Discovering Pathomechanisms and Novel Drug Optimization for AMD). Subretinal mononuclear phagocytes (MPs) build up in the photoreceptor cell layer, a zone normally kept free of immune cells by the immunosuppressive retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). This build-up is a key driver of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). MPs include microglia and monocyte-derived inflammatory macrophages (MoMφ). Our team has shown that activated MPs evade RPE-mediated clearance. We have also shown that the AMD-linked CFH 402H variant impairs the removal of subretinal MPs independently of its role in the complement system. How complement dysregulation contributes to immune cell accumulation in the subretinal space in AMD remains poorly understood. The PhD student will first map where complement cascade components are found in the human retina. Using multiplexed immunohistochemistry on post-mortem retinal sections from AMD donors and age-matched controls, the student will localise components of the classical, lectin and alternative pathways, their activation products, regulators (CFH and Factor H-related proteins) and receptors. These components will be mapped relative to subretinal MPs, the RPE, photoreceptors and drusen. The student will then study how the Chromosome 1 (Chr1) AMD risk haplotype affects RPE, microglia and MoMφ and their interactions. They will use control and Chr1-risk iPSC-derived cells in a well-defined co-culture system developed in our laboratory. The student will also study the role of plasma-derived Factor H-related proteins (FHR1-5) using depleted human plasma and purified complement factors. Using single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing and proteomics, the student will analyse how complement dysregulation affects: microglia and MoMφ polarisation the interaction of these cells with the immunosuppressive RPE key inflammatory pathways and immune functions in the subretinal microenvironment, in health and in AMD Finally, the student will test whether complement inhibitors (anti-C5, anti-C3) can restore immune balance. The project is supervised by Dr. Florian Sennlaub (Institut de la Vision, Paris) It is carried out in close collaboration with other PANDORA doctoral candidates. Techniques and Training Include: Multiplexed immunohistochemistry on human donor retinal sections (AMD and age-matched controls), whole-slide/confocal imaging and quantitative image analysis Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived RPE, microglia and macrophage models, and immune cell/RPE co-cultures Primary human monocyte isolation and differentiation, and work with human plasma and purified complement factors Single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, and proteomics Flow cytometry, qPCR, western blot, ELISA/multiplex cytokine assays Functional immune assays (phagocytosis, migration, survival/clearance) Prise de fonction : 01/02/2027 Nature du financement Financement de l'Union européenne Précisions sur le financement Horizon Europe – MSCA (Marie Curie Actions) Présentation établissement et labo d'accueil Sorbonne Université Founded by Professor José-Alain Sahel, the Institut de la Vision is an international research centre dedicated entirely to research into eye and vision diseases. It brings together researchers, doctors, patients and industry on the same site to discover innovative treatments for eye diseases and improve the quality of life of visually impaired people. It is being built on a site that brings together l’Hôpital national de la vision des 15-20 and its Clinical Investigation Centre (CIC), as well as the Centre for Rare Retinal Diseases. Designed as a place where people can come together and exchange ideas, the Institut de la Vision enables ideas to be shared, new questions to emerge and the transfer of research findings to patient care to be accelerated. Its innovative organisation, based around hospital patients, enables new therapeutic or technological solutions to be discovered, tested and developed in order to prevent eye diseases or limit their effects. More than 300 researchers are working in the 5 research departments of the Institut de la Vision: developmental biology of the visual system, genetics, visual information processing, pathophysiology and therapeutics, photonics. All the Institut de la Vision's activities and projects are coordinated by its Foundation (Foundation Institut de la vision), in conjunction with its three supervisory bodies: Sorbonne University, Inserm and the CNRS. Site web : http://www.institut-vision.org Profil du candidat Education Level: Master's Degree or equivalent in life sciences, biology, immunology, neurobiology or biomedical sciences Essential Skills/Qualifications: Solid knowledge of cellular and molecular biology and/or immunology Excellent written and oral English proficiency Strong motivation for research on retinal degeneration and neuroinflammation Ability to work both in a team and independently Preferred Qualifications: Hands-on experience in cell culture (ideally primary immune cells or iPSC-derived cells) and flow cytometry Experience with immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence and image analysis Background in innate immunity, macrophage/microglia biology and the complement system Interest in, or basic experience with, omics data analysis Language: Excellent English (French not required) Applicants must meet these requirements: They must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in France for more than 12 months in the 36 months before the recruitment date. Compulsory national service and time spent in refugee status procedures are excluded. They must not already hold a doctoral degree. They can be of any nationality. items.title: PhD: Impact evaluation of climate policies in agricultural and forest landscapes
items.desc: Your job Have you ever wondered how we can ensure that climate mitigation and adaptation policies are fair, coherent, and effective? Are you interested in applying state-of-the-art impact evaluation techniques to analyze how climate policies affect land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity? Do you good communication skills in Spanish? Then this might be your next step! Climate change mitigation and adaptation in agriculture and forestry represent a “wicked problem”, shaped by uncertainty, conflicting objectives, institutional fragmentation and time pressure. While the EU has set ambitious climate targets for 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050, progress in agriculture and forestry remains insufficient and current policy frameworks have not yet resulted in significant climate mitigation and adaptation results, or generated the systemic transformation needed. This PhD position is part of the EU-Horizon project “ Evidence-based pathways towards fair, coherent and effective climate policies for Europe’s agriculture and forestry (PolicyForClimate) ”, which will develop tools and frameworks to enable policymakers and other stakeholders to design fair, coherent, and effective climate mitigation and adaptation policies in the EU. The project will use AI-assisted evidence synthesis, a policy-lab approach, and embedded case studies to offer a continuously updated evidence base on policy impacts, trade-offs, synergies, and spillovers. Your research will focus on developing, applying, and validating a novel mixed-methods framework for ex-post impact evaluation of climate policies in forestry and agricultural landscapes. By combining state-of-the-art econometric techniques with qualitative participatory approaches, you will empirically analyze how climate policies have affected land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity metrics. This will require conducting systematic reviews on existing impact evaluation frameworks, run workshops and focus group discussions with various stakeholders, collect, combine, and analyze farm-level primary data and secondary spatially explicit data. Start date: February 2027. Your duties and responsibilities include: Conduct systematic literature reviews and workshops to develop a mixed-methods ex-post impact evaluation framework for climate policies; Apply rigorous econometric methods together with qualitative assessments , particularly from policy sciences, to evaluate the impact of specific climate policies on land cover, carbon, and biodiversity metrics; Conduct focus group discussions with various stakeholders in the EU to validate the proposed impact evaluation framework and results from the empirical analyses; Write research papers and present research findings at international academic conferences; Collaborate with our research partners and contribute to the dissemination of project results . You will work here You will be based at the Forest and Nature Conservation Policy Group (FNP) at Wageningen University . The FNP group focuses on the political, socio-economic and cultural dimensions of forests and nature. Our research addresses major challenges including biodiversity conservation, deforestation, forest transitions, climate change and landscape management in both the Global North and Global South. You will be jointly supervised by Dr. Jorge Sellare and Prof. Bas Arts from Wageningen University (WU-FNP), and by Dr. Dario Schulz (EFI) in the research group headed by Sven Wunder. Your qualities We are looking for a researcher with a strong interest in climate adaptation and mitigation policies and in exploring the underlying causal mechanisms through which they affect land, GHG emissions, and biodiversity. You enjoy working with both quantitative and qualitative data and are motivated to conduct research that combines rigorous econometric analysis with qualitative assessments and with real-world challenges facing farmers and forest owners. Fieldwork in Spain will be an important component of the PhD project, so Spanish language skills are critical. You should be enthusiastic about working with farmers and able to spend time in rural areas of Spain under fieldwork conditions. You also possess: a successfully completed MSc degree in agricultural economics, environmental economics, environmental policy, forestry or a closely related field; affinity with applied econometrics and / or qualitative mixed methods and an interest in developing your skills in both; knowledge of GIS and spatial data analysis is an asset; good skills with statistical software such as R, Stata or Python; very good communication skills in Spanish (min. level B2); For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level. Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here. We offer Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment. A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include: Partially paid parental leave; working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance; there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee; a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%; excellent pension scheme. In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team. The gross salary for the first year is € 3.204,- per month rising to € 4.051,- in the fourth year in according to the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (scale P). This is based on a full-time working week of 38 hours. We offer a temporary contract for 18 months which will be extended for the duration of the project if you perform well. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help. You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment. Coming from abroad Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. items.title: PhD in Acoustic Performance of Timber Structure Connections
items.desc: Sustainability, in its broadest definition, is the cornerstone of research and education in the Department of Built Environment. We take the lead in (re)shaping the built environment to be future-proof, safe, healthy, inclusive and respectful of planetary boundaries. We house the entire spectrum of technology, engineering, design, and human behavior disciplines in the built environment, with world-class experimental facilities at all scales. This allows us to address societal challenges from a uniquely integrated perspective. Introduction Are you fascinated by improving the acoustic performance of timber buildings? Help develop advanced numerical models that predict sound transmission and bridge the gap between sustainable construction and high acoustic performance. Join this joint PhD project between TU/e and DTU! Job Description Buildings made from timber and other biobased materials generally have a significantly lower carbon footprint than conventional concrete or masonry constructions. However, lightweight timber structures often exhibit high variability in sound insulation, and poor acoustic performance remains a barrier to their wider adoption in the construction industry. A still poorly understood source of this variability lies in the connections between structural components, such as screws, nails, steel brackets, and adhesive joints. Whether a floor is screwed or glued together, and how widely spaced the fasteners are, can significantly affect how sound travels through a building. Current prediction methods largely ignore these details, while more detailed models are often too computationally expensive for practical use. Developing methods that are both physically accurate and computationally efficient is therefore the central challenge of this project. We offer a PhD position (4-year contract) within the QUIET-ARC project, a collaboration between Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as part of the EuroTech Universities PhD programme. As a PhD candidate in the QUIET-ARC project, you will investigate how different connection types and layouts influence sound transmission in timber buildings, develop efficient numerical simulation methods to model these effects, and quantify the uncertainty introduced by construction variability into acoustic predictions. Noise is recognised by the World Health Organisation as a major public health concern. By improving the predictive capability of computational models for timber buildings, this research supports more reliable prediction tools for sustainable constructions and contributes to the wider adoption of low-carbon building materials. The project will take place under joint supervision of dr.ir. Cédric Van hoorickx (TU/e, specializing in numerical modelling of sound transmission) and dr.ir. Jonas Brunskog (DTU, with expertise in the acoustics of lightweight structures). You will be based in the Building Acoustics research group (https://building-acoustics.net/) in the Department of the Built Environment at TU/e, and will spend approximately six months at DTU’s Acoustic Technology group in Denmark. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in acoustics, building physics, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, or related disciplines. A research-oriented attitude. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). The following experience could be considered an advantage and may be highlighted in your motivation letter: Affinity for building acoustics, vibro-acoustics, or structural dynamics Previous experience with/affinity for computational methods Previous publications and scientific communications Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here. items.title: PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on ML-methods in climate modelling
items.desc: The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain. We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic. The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment. You can read more about us here: the Department of Meteorology. Project description Clouds and their responses to varying environmental conditions are particularly important determinants of current climate and future climate change. However, the resolution of a typical climate model is far too coarse to explicitly represent processes of relevance to cloud formation. Those processes therefore need to be parameterized, or represented as functions of large-scale state variables. Such sub-grid scale parameterizations are associated with large uncertainties, and are also computationally expensive. This project focuses on novel ways to bridge between micro- and global scales, to improve climate model accuracy, efficiency and generalizability, and leverage modern computer architecture. We will explore the use of machine learning (ML) models trained on combinations of observational data and high-resolution simulations, as alternatives to empirical parameterizations of essential, unresolved sub-grid scale processes related to turbulence, cloud formation and aerosol-cloud interaction. The tasks will include deriving and training data-driven models, coupling them to a large-scale climate model, evaluating the results against observations and traditionally parameterized models, and using the ML-enhanced model to estimate climate-relevant quantities like cloud radiative effects and forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with data scientists within the Swedish e-Science Research Centre, and contribute to development of methods with applicability also beyond climate science. The successful candidate will thereby develop their skills in atmospheric science and climate modelling, but also in data science and machine learning, and in communicating and collaborating within and across disciplines. Qualification requirements In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be fulfilled before admission to the programme. You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. The specific entry requirements additionally require a minimum of 90 higher education credits in any of the fields of meteorology, oceanography, physics or chemistry; and at least 15 higher education credits in mathematics as well as a degree project of at least 15 higher education credits. At least 60 higher education credits of these courses must be on the second-cycle level. In addition, proficiency in English language, equivalent to English B in Swedish high school, is required. The specific entry requirements may also be fulfilled by a person who has otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. General syllabus for doctoral studies in atmospheric science and oceanography. Selection The selection between candidates who meet the entry requirements will be made with reference to their ability to benefit from the training. However, the fact that an applicant is deemed able to transfer credits from previous training or professional experience may not alone give the applicant priority over other applicants in the selection process. Admission decisions are made in accordance with current delegation policies. The assessment criteria for admission to the postgraduate programme in atmospheric sciences and oceanography are familiarity with the theory and applications of the subject, subject knowledge relevant to the research project, the ability to express oneself orally and in writing, proficiency in English, analytical ability, creativity, initiative, independence and the ability to work collaboratively. The assessment of the applicant’s ability in these respects are based on the relevance and results of completed higher education courses, the quality and scope of the independent project, references, interviews and a personal statement from the applicant describing their expectations of, and intentions regarding, the programme. Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University. About the employment Starting date as per agreement. We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %). A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. Stockholm University strives to be a workplace free from discrimination and with equal opportunities for all. Contact For more information about the project, please contact professor Frida Bender, frida.bender@misu.su.se. For more information about the PhD programme, please contact the study director, Associate Professor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. For information about the recruitment process and terms of employment, please contact Head of Administration Sara Engström, sara.engstrom@misu.su.se. It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the job advertisement, and that it is submitted before the deadline. We kindly ask applicants to refrain from submitting AI-generated applications. The instructions for applicants are available at: How to apply for a position. items.title: Industrial PhD Student in AI
items.desc: INDUSTRIAL PHD STUDENT IN AI, Sundsvall Would you like to turn deep research into real impact in the factory, in our products and in the lives of the people who use them? At Permobil, we’re looking for game-changers to join us as we innovate for individuals and develop the world’s most advanced assistive solutions. At Permobil , the people who use our products come first. Our purpose is to create advanced assistive solutions that make the lives of adults and children living with disabilities more enriching. Our people are passionate about pushing the boundaries of technology to deliver innovations that improve lives. We are a sustainable and responsible business committed to continuous improvement, and our customers can trust us to provide market-leading solutions driven by insights-based clinical data. At Permobil in Sundsvall, we design and manufacture power wheelchairs and Panthera manual wheelchairs. Sundsvall is one of our largest and most modern sites, with production, R&D and clinical research side by side. About the role Permobil is now establishing an industrial PhD position in artificial intelligence , in close collaboration with Mid Sweden University (Mittuniversitetet) . The position is part of a four-year research project and gives you the chance to do doctoral research with one foot in academia and one foot in a real industrial environment. As Industrial PhD Student, you will be employed by Permobil in Sundsvall and admitted to the doctoral program at Mid Sweden University. You will work with the large amounts of operational and product data that our organization generates every day, and build deep knowledge about how AI can create value from it for our operations, our products and the people who use them. The research problem is deliberately open. Rather than a narrowly defined task, you get room to explore, ask deeper questions and shape the research direction together with your academic supervisors and your colleagues at Permobil. Key responsibilities: Plan and carry out doctoral research in applied AI, and complete your doctoral studies and thesis within the project period, Define and refine the research questions together with your supervisors as the project evolves, Work with real operational and product data from Permobil and turn it into new knowledge, Develop, test and evaluate AI methods, and show how they perform in a real industrial setting, Take part in doctoral courses and in the research environment at Mid Sweden University, Publish and present your results at conferences and in journals, in dialogue with Permobil and in line with the project agreement, Share insights and build competence with colleagues in Operations, R&D, Clinical and other functions at the site. items.title: PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on mixed-phase cloud processes
items.desc: The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain. We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic. The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment. Read more about us here: the Department of Meteorology. Project description Clouds regulate how much sunlight reaches the Earth’s surface and how much thermal radiation escapes to space, which ultimately influences how hot or cold the planet is. How much each cloud cools or warms the Earth depends in part on its composition. Is it made up of liquid particles, ice particles, or both? How densely spaced and how large are these particles? The answers to these questions lie partially in the dynamics occurring within the cloud. Even clouds that look calm from the ground may generate motions strong enough to shake an airplane. These motions can form new cloud particles and combine or shatter existing ones. However, these motions are difficult to represent completely in computer models of the atmosphere and in laboratory experiments, and we have yet to understand their full impact. The PhD student will build this understanding using over 800 hours of wind and cloud particle measurements that have been recorded by specialized research aircraft during field campaigns run by government agencies in the US and Europe. Data have been collected over the midwestern US and the Caribbean, off the northwestern coast of Africa, between Australia and Antarctica, and in the vicinity of Svalbard. Quality-controlled versions of all data are already available, so analysis can begin at the project start.The PhD student will develop a detailed understanding of aircraft instrumentation through literature review and apply that expertise to the analysis of measurements from dozens of different aircraft-mounted instruments. All analysis will be done in Python. The scientific scope initially spans micrometer-scale cloud particles to the dynamical processes that affect clouds, including turbulent eddies and kilometer-scale atmospheric waves. Initial science questions are well defined and focus on identifying statistical relationships between cloud particle properties and cloud-scale dynamics, and investigating how these vary across cloud types and geographic regions. After the initial stage, the project is more open-ended. The PhD student may choose to focus on the same micrometer–kilometer scales, or to make connections between these scales and the regional or global climate. They may also choose to branch into atmospheric modelling and/or to use machine learning to model observed relationships between cloud dynamics and cloud particles. Qualification requirements In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be met by the deadline for applications. You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. The specific entry requirements comprise a minimum of 90 higher education credits in one of the subjects meteorology, oceanography, physics or chemistry, at least 15 higher education credits in mathematics, as well as an independent degree project of at least 15 higher education credits. Furthermore, English language proficiency equivalent to English 6/English Level 2 at upper secondary school is required. The specific entry requirements may also be met by those who have acquired equivalent knowledge through other means, either in Sweden or abroad. General syllabus for doctoral studies in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography. Selection Selection from among applicants who meet the entry requirements shall be made with regards to their ability to benefit from the programme. That fact alone that an applicant is assessed to be able to receive credits for previous educational or professional/vocational activities to be credited to the educational programme may not give the applicant priority over other applicants in the selection process. Decisions on admission are made in accordance with the applicable delegation regulations. The assessment criteria for admission to the postgraduate programme in atmospheric sciences and oceanography are familiarity with the theory and applications of the subject, subject knowledge relevant to the research project, the ability to express oneself orally and in writing, proficiency in English, analytical ability, creativity, initiative, independence and the ability to work collaboratively. Prior Python experience is desirable but not required. The assessment of the applicant’s ability in these respects are based on the relevance and results of completed higher education courses, the quality and scope of the independent project, references, interviews and a personal statement from the applicant describing their expectations of, and intentions regarding, the programme. Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University. About the employment Starting date is flexible, as per agreement, but preferably not before 1 February 2027. We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %). A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. Stockholm University strives to be a workplace free from discrimination and with equal opportunities for all. Contact For more information about the project, please contact Assistant Professor Rachel Atlas, rachel.atlas@misu.su.se. For more information about the PhD programme, please contact the study director, Associate Professor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. For information about the recruitment process and terms of employment, please contact Head of Administration Sara Engström, sara.engstrom@misu.su.se. It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the job advertisement, and that it is submitted before the deadline.
