items.title: PhD student in Geophysics
items.desc: PhD student in Geophysics: Enhancing exploration drilling efficiency through integrated analyses rock formation and drilling data Are you interested in working with sustainable and responsible exploration drilling of critical raw materials, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University. The Department of Earth Sciences is Sweden's most comprehensive academic environment for research and education in geoscience. It offers a broad range of expertise that can contribute to solving important societal issues. Earth is a dynamic and constantly changing planet. To understand how this planet works, our researchers seek answers in the field, through laboratory experiments and advanced models. Our research and education cover a wide range of disciplines, including rocks and minerals, weather and climate, the evolution of life, natural disasters, wind power and energy, environmental and water engineering, and sustainable development. Our research combines natural sciences and technology with social sciences and is often interdisciplinary. More than 300 people from over 30 countries work at the department, both in Uppsala and at Campus Gotland. Our six research divisions: Geophysics • Air, Water and Landscape Science • Mineralogy, Petrology and Tectonics Natural Resources and Sustainable Development • Palaeobiology • Wind Energy For more information see: www.uu.se/earthsciences Geophysics is about "looking into" and understanding the Earth’s structure, its history and processes-based on measurements of the Earth’s physical properties. In geophysics we use quantitative physical methods to investigate the Earth and its environment. In addition, physical property measurements, rock mechanical field testing, scientific drilling and numerical modelling are employed to investigate the subsurface structures and processes. The Geophysics program currently runs several national and international projects and has a wealth of world-class infrastructures. It also leads the Smart Exploration Research Center (SERC) (www.smartexploration.se). SERC is funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research, with members from four Swedish universities, three mining companies, four technology companies, and one development company. The PhD project will be conducted in close collaboration with Epiroc, Nordic Iron and Lund University. In this PhD project, you will be enrolled as a PhD student at Uppsala University in close collaboration with Epiroc Rock Drills AB in Örebro. You will mainly be placed at Uppsala University, Uppsala. During shorter periods, you will also be placed at Epiroc Rock Drills AB in Örebro and participate if field work. Access to certain technology or data associated with industry partners within the project may be subject to applicable export control legislation and will be managed in accordance with current regulations. Duties The PhD candidate will conduct research within SERC, focusing on sustainable and responsible exploration of critical raw materials. The overarching aim of the PhD project is to develop a framework for integrating rock formation and drilling data to improve exploration drilling efficiency, thereby contribute to more sustainable and responsible exploration drilling. The project combines geoscience and drilling technology, with a focus on diamond core drilling in crystalline rock. The PhD candidate will develop advanced theoretical, technical and practical expertise in the technical and operational challenges of the drilling process, as well as geoscientific methods for subsurface characterization. The work involves data acquisition in connection with exploration drilling, borehole logging, in-situ testing, drill core analyses, and laboratory testing. Separate and integrated analyses of these datasets will be used to investigate potential relationships between rock formation properties, drilling data, and exploration drilling efficiency. The doctoral student will work in close collaboration with academic and industry research groups contributing to stronger collaboration and knowledge exchange between these communities. The PhD candidate is expected to combine theoretical and practical work, work both independently and collaboratively, spend parts of the project period with industry partners, and participate in field and laboratory work. Requirements To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must: hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in geophysics, geology, rock mechanics, drilling technology, physics, earth sciences or a similar field, or have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way. We are seeking a candidate with strong interests in exploration drilling in crystalline rocks and methods for subsurface characterisation, both in-situ and in the laboratory. Good oral and written proficiency in English is required. Additional qualifications Experience in various types of data acquisition and analysis, such as measurement while drilling (MWD), logging while drilling (LWD), borehole logging, rock stress measurements, drill core logging, and rock mechanic laboratory testing, is considered a merit. Experience in integrating and analysing different types of drilling data, rock formation data, or a combination of these is also considered a merit. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively is considered a merit. Proficiency in spoken and written Swedish is a merit, because communication in Swedish may be required during fieldwork and collaboration with industry partners. A driving license is a merit, as it may be required for fieldwork. Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines. A PhD position is full-time for four years. Teaching or administrative duties at the department corresponding to a maximum of 20 per cent may occur by agreement. The employment is extended to a corresponding extent. Application A personal letter describing yourself, your research interests, why you wish to pursue doctoral studies, and why you are a suitable candidate for this specific position and project (maximum 2 pages). A curriculum vitae (CV). A verified transcript of records and a brief description of your educational background. A copy of your Master's degree certificate (or equivalent advanced-level degree certificate). Your degree project/thesis report (finished or in draft form). Names and contact details of two references (including email addresses and telephone numbers). About the employment The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting date 15 January 2027, or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala For further information about the position, please contact: Assoc. Prof. Maria Ask, phone: +46 18 471 3509, e-mail: maria.ask@geo.uu.se. Please submit your application by 3 November 2026, UFV-PA 2026/ 3081 . Are you considering moving to Sweden to work at Uppsala University? Find out more about what it´s like to work and live in Sweden. Uppsala University is a broad research university with a strong international position. The ultimate goal is to conduct education and research of the highest quality and relevance to make a difference in society. Our most important asset is all of our 7,500 employees and 53,000 students who, with curiosity and commitment, make Uppsala University one of Sweden’s most exciting workplaces. Read more about our benefits and what it is like to work at Uppsala Universityhttps://uu.se/om-uu/jobba-hos-oss/ The position may be subject to security vetting. If security vetting is conducted, the applicant must pass the vetting process to be eligible for employment. Please do not send offers of recruitment or advertising services. Submit your application through Uppsala University's recruitment system. items.title: PhD Student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on aerosol-cloud-climate interactions
items.desc: Meteorologiska institutionen vid Stockholms universitet (MISU) bedriver forskning och utbildning som rör atmosfären, oceanen, och fysikaliskt-baserad klimatvetenskap. MISU erbjuder utbildningsprogram på kandidat-, master- och forskarnivå. Vår forskning söker svar på grundläggande frågor om atmosfärens och havens dynamiska, fysiska, kemiska, och biogeokemiska egenskaper av relevans för väder och klimat. Vi strävar efter en bred forskningsverksamhet inom vårt vetenskapliga område. Vi studerar frågor som sträcker sig från djuphavet till den övre atmosfären och från tropikerna till polerna. I vår forskning utnyttjar och utvecklar vi teori, statistiska metoder och numeriska modeller i nära samspel med observationer. Dessutom utvecklar och leder institutionen observationsbaserad forskning med stöd av satelliter, arktiska isbrytarexpeditioner och landbaserade instrument. MISU har cirka 60 anställda och ingår i en större forskningsmiljö som inkluderar Bolincentret för klimatforskning, Östersjöcentrum och Swedish e-Science Research Centre. Institutionen har stark internationell prägel, över hälften av medarbetarna har en bakgrund utanför Sverige och både svenska och engelska används som arbetsspråk. Vi välkomnar och värdesätter mångfald i vår arbetsmiljö. Mer information om oss finns att läsa på: Meteorologiska institutionen. Projektbeskrivning Samspelet mellan aerosolpartiklar och moln utgör en potentiellt betydande, men fortfarande mycket osäker, faktor i klimatförändringarna. Projektet syftar till att öka förståelsen för hur aerosolföroreningar påverkar moln som består av vattendroppar. Inom projektet ges möjlighet att undersöka detta genom att testa en ny teori som förutspår att aerosolföroreningar förstärker uppvindarna i konvektiva moln, vilket kan göra molnen tjockare och mer reflekterande. Det finns även möjlighet att studera trender i jordens strålningsbudget kopplade till aerosol-moln-interaktioner under satelliteran. Forskningsarbetet kan omfatta både numeriska simuleringar och analys av satellitdata. Behörighetskrav För att bli antagen till forskarutbildning krävs att den sökande har grundläggande och särskild behörighet. Behörigheten ska vara uppfylld senast sista ansökningsdag. Grundläggande behörighet har du, om du avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng (hp), varav minst 60 hp på avancerad nivå, eller på annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. För särskild behörighet krävs minst 90 hp i något av ämnena meteorologi, oceanografi, fysik eller kemi, minst 15 hp i matematik och ett självständigt arbete om minst 15 hp. Av detta skall minst 60 hp vara på avancerad nivå. Vidare krävs språkkunskaper i engelska motsvarande engelska B på gymnasiet. Allmän studieplan för studier på forskarnivå i atmosfärsvetenskap och oceanografi. Urval Urval bland de sökande som uppfyller behörighetskraven ska göras med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig utbildningen. Enbart det förhållandet att en sökande bedöms kunna få tidigare utbildning eller yrkesverksamhet tillgodoräknad för utbildningen får inte vid urval ge sökanden företräde framför andra sökande. Beslut om antagning fattas enligt gällande delegationsordning. Vid bedömningen tas hänsyn till förtrogenhet och skicklighet inom ämnet, förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på engelska, analytisk förmåga, kreativitet, initiativförmåga och självständighet, och samarbetsförmåga. Till grund för bedömningen ligger tidigare studiers relevans, betyg på genomgångna högskolekurser (särskilt de på avancerad nivå), kvalitet och omfattning på det självständiga arbetet, referenser, intervjuer samt skriftlig avsiktsförklaring. Antagningsordning för utbildning på forskarnivå vid Stockholms universitet. Om anställningen Tillträde den 1 januari 2027 eller enligt överenskommelse. Vi erbjuder en tidsbegränsad anställning som doktorand enligt 5 kap. högskoleförordningen (1993:100). Anställningstiden får inte vara längre än vad som motsvarar utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid under fyra år. Som doktorand ska du främst ägna dig åt din egen utbildning på forskarnivå, men i anställningen kan arbete med utbildning, forskning och administration ingå i begränsad omfattning (högst 20 %). En ny anställning som doktorand gäller för högst ett år, anställningen förnyas därefter med högst två år i taget. items.title: PhD position in biomineralization of digitally fabricated granular materials
items.desc: Mission We are offering a challenging position as a full-time (100%) PhD Student in the Laloui Group at EPFL inLausanne. The group brings expertise in geomaterials and their mechanical behaviour to research at theinterface of material science and engineering applications. You will work on the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)-funded project “DFabuLis: Digital FabricationUsing Living Systems”, conducted in collaboration between Dr. Dimitrios Terzis, Senior Scientist in the LalouiGroup at EPFL, and co-PI Prof. Benjamin Dillenburger of the Chair of Digital Building Technologies at ETHZurich. The project investigates how biologically driven mineralization can transform demolition and excavationmaterials into materials suitable for digital fabrication under ambient conditions. Digital fabrication methods, including extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying, offer opportunities to controlmaterial placement and curing, create complex geometries and reduce material consumption. Integratingbiomineralization into pumpable, extrudable and sprayable granular materials remains largely unexplored. ThisPhD will investigate the coupled biogeochemical, rheological and mechanical mechanisms governing particledeposition, mineral precipitation and hardening. Main duties and responsibilities As a PhD Student, you will be expected to: Take full responsibility for your dissertation and the progress of your research. Conduct research in close collaboration with project partners at EPFL and ETH Zurich and, whereapplicable, industry partners. Design and execute experiments, and analyze and interpret experimental results. Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present your findings at internationalconferences. Participate in teaching and supervise student projects. More specifically, within this project, you will: Investigate the rheology and processability of granular materials, including yield stress, plastic viscosity,thixotropy, water content, ageing and particle interactions. Study microbial activity and biologically driven mineral precipitation, and determine how evolving mineralphases affect mechanical hardening and material performance. Characterize the coupling between biogeochemical reactions, rheological properties and mechanicalbehaviour over space and time. Connect experimental findings to extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying in collaboration with thedigital fabrication team at ETH Zurich. Profile An MSc degree in Civil Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering or aclosely related discipline. A background in mechanics and the strength of solid materials, or materials science applied to the builtenvironment, is particularly welcome. Experience in rheology, granular or cementitious materials, experimental mechanics, materialcharacterization, geomechanics, mineralogy, or organic and inorganic chemistry is an advantage.Expertise across all these fields is neither expected nor required. Interest in experimental and interdisciplinary research, and in translating fundamental physical andchemical understanding into new construction technologies. Good communication skills and willingness to work as part of a team across disciplines and institutions. IDHEAP is the largest university institute in Switzerland dedicated entirely and exclusively to the public sector. We offer excellent research support in a dynamic public policy and public administration research community and are committed to promoting the careers of young scholars. Are you interested in the future of AI and the algorithmic state? Are you enthusiastic about developing research at the crossroads between Public Management and Information Systems? Join our research team in the project “Beyond the Gig Economy: Exploring the New Frontiers of Algorithmic Control”. The project examines the implications and different design alternatives of algorithms gradually replacing human decision-making. The ideal candidate is therefore sensitive to technical and social questions and interested in conducting challenging empirical work in a fast-moving environment. Industrial PhD Student in AI
items.desc: INDUSTRIAL PHD STUDENT IN AI, Sundsvall Would you like to turn deep research into real impact in the factory, in our products and in the lives of the people who use them? At Permobil, we’re looking for game-changers to join us as we innovate for individuals and develop the world’s most advanced assistive solutions. At Permobil , the people who use our products come first. Our purpose is to create advanced assistive solutions that make the lives of adults and children living with disabilities more enriching. Our people are passionate about pushing the boundaries of technology to deliver innovations that improve lives. We are a sustainable and responsible business committed to continuous improvement, and our customers can trust us to provide market-leading solutions driven by insights-based clinical data. At Permobil in Sundsvall, we design and manufacture power wheelchairs and Panthera manual wheelchairs. Sundsvall is one of our largest and most modern sites, with production, R&D and clinical research side by side. About The Role Permobil is now establishing an industrial PhD position in artificial intelligence , in close collaboration with Mid Sweden University (Mittuniversitetet) . The position is part of a four-year research project and gives you the chance to do doctoral research with one foot in academia and one foot in a real industrial environment. As Industrial PhD Student, you will be employed by Permobil in Sundsvall and admitted to the doctoral program at Mid Sweden University. You will work with the large amounts of operational and product data that our organization generates every day, and build deep knowledge about how AI can create value from it for our operations, our products and the people who use them. The research problem is deliberately open. Rather than a narrowly defined task, you get room to explore, ask deeper questions and shape the research direction together with your academic supervisors and your colleagues at Permobil. Key Responsibilities Plan and carry out doctoral research in applied AI, and complete your doctoral studies and thesis within the project period, Define and refine the research questions together with your supervisors as the project evolves, Work with real operational and product data from Permobil and turn it into new knowledge, Develop, test and evaluate AI methods, and show how they perform in a real industrial setting, Take part in doctoral courses and in the research environment at Mid Sweden University, Publish and present your results at conferences and in journals, in dialogue with Permobil and in line with the project agreement, Share insights and build competence with colleagues in Operations, R&D, Clinical and other functions at the site. Skills & Qualifications Basic eligibility for doctoral studies: a degree at advanced level, or completed course requirements of at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits at advanced level, or equivalent knowledge acquired in Sweden or abroad, Specific eligibility: at least 90 credits in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science or closely related subjects, Good command of English, spoken and written. Swedish is an advantage, Experience in machine learning, data analysis or industrial applications of AI is an advantage, but not a requirement, Comfortable working in an international company and in a cross-functional context. Who Are You You are curious, driven and goal-oriented, with a strong interest in turning research into practical value. You like to ask the deeper question rather than settle for the first answer, and you are comfortable moving between the data, the shop floor and the clinic. You create an environment where people feel safe to share ideas, challenge assumptions and learn together. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively with others and take ownership of your work. You share our belief in respect for people and continuous improvement. What We Offer A rare opportunity for both technical and personal development: doctoral education at Mid Sweden University combined with work on real industrial and product data at one of Permobil’s most modern sites. You get close support from supervisors at both the university and Permobil, and the chance to see your research put to use in a company with a clear purpose and a strong belief in the future. Application Process We will conduct selection continuously so send us your application today or before 20th of November at the latest! The position is based in Sundsvall, with a project period of four years. Permobil is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals. For more information about the position, please contact Mikael Boija, Senior Director Operational Excellence, mikael.boija@permobil.com For information about the recruitment process, please contact Zivile Mitkute, Talent Acquisition Partner, zivile.mitkute@permobil.com Please respect that we do not wish recruitment assistance or advertising, we decline calls from recruitment and advertising providers. More About Permobil Permobil founder Dr. Per Uddén believed that helping people achieve the greatest level of independence is a basic human right and, for over 50 years, Permobil has held fast to that belief. Permobil is a global leader in advanced rehabilitation technology, passionate about better understanding our users’ needs and improving their quality of life through state-of-the-art healthcare solutions. Today, those solutions include power wheelchairs, seating and positioning products, power assist, and manual wheelchairs. Permobil is part of Patricia Industries, a subsidiary of Investor AB, and is headquartered in Sweden. Permobil has 2 000 team members in 18 countries around the world. For more information regarding the company’s storied history and complete product line, visit permobil.com.

items.title: PhD Scholarship in Machine Learning for Non-Stationary and Non-Static Nano-Tomography - DTU Compute
items.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
items.desc: Job Description Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial resolution, even minute positioning errors, mechanical drift, and sample deformations become sources of image degradation. The central challenge is to reconstruct accurate 3D and 4D representations of samples while accounting for positional uncertainties during image acquisition and changes in sample shape over time. The project will bring together neural representations, inverse problems, geometric modeling, and computational imaging to address fundamental challenges in nano-tomography. Rather than correcting acquisition errors and sample deformations as separate preprocessing steps, you will investigate how to model and estimate the sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation jointly from the measured data. The position is based at DTU Compute and conducted in close collaboration with EPFL and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland, one of the leading centers for synchrotron X-ray imaging. As a PhD student, you will work in an international research environment spanning DTU, EPFL, and PSI, combining expertise in both machine learning and computational imaging with access to experimental data and advanced imaging facilities. Research visits to Switzerland are planned as part of the project. Responsibilities Develop novel machine learning and deep learning methods for X-ray nano-tomography, which jointly reconstruct sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation fields from inconsistent projection data. Investigate neural field representations for 3D and 4D imaging, including models that capture changes in sample geometry over time, and explore hybrid approaches combining learning-based methods with physical models of image formation and tomographic reconstruction. Validate and evaluate the developed methods using experimental nano-tomography data, initially focusing on integrated circuits. Collaborate with researchers at DTU, PSI, and EPFL, and participate in international research visits and scientific activities. Publish research results in leading journals and conferences in machine learning, computer vision, and computational imaging. Contribute to research-based teaching and supervision of MSc and BSc student projects. Participate in activities within the Center for Quantification of Imaging Data from MAX IV (QIM), including workshops, training courses, and interdisciplinary research collaborations. Qualifications You are curious and motivated by developing new machine learning methods to solve challenging problems in computational imaging. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning is particularly important. We welcome candidates from computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, and related disciplines who are interested in combining modern learning methods with mathematical modeling and real-world experimental data. The candidate should be able to work independently, contribute effectively to an interdisciplinary research team, and communicate scientific ideas clearly in written and spoken English. To succeed in this position, you are expected to have: A master's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning, including experience developing, implementing, or evaluating learning-based models. Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, and familiarity with relevant machine learning frameworks. A solid understanding of mathematical modeling, optimization, or numerical methods. Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: Neural representations, implicit neural fields, or other coordinate-based representations. Computer vision, 3D vision, geometric modeling, or structure-from-motion. Inverse problems, image reconstruction, or physics-informed machine learning. Image registration, motion estimation, or deformable modeling. Image processing, image analysis, or tomographic reconstruction. Knowledge of X-ray imaging and tomography is beneficial but not required. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation. At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 March 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Hans Martin Kjer, hmkj@dtu.dk . You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 16 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time) . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file . The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. DTU Compute DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk . DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

items.title: Promotionsstelle an der UTN im Bereich Mathematische Optimierung für Multi-Roboter-Systeme (m/w/d)
items.desc: for english version, see below - Die Technische Universität Nürnberg (UTN) bietet eine inspirierende und interdisziplinäre Forschungsumgebung mit Zugang zu modernsten Ressourcen. Sie ist der ideale Ort, um zukunftsträchtige Entdeckungen zu machen und einen bedeutenden Beitrag zu spannenden Forschungsfeldern zu leisten. Promotionsstelle an der UTN im Bereich Mathematische Optimierung für Multi-Roboter-Systeme (m/w/d) Das Department Liberal Arts & Social Sciences bietet derzeit eine Promotionsstelle (vollfinanziert, 3 Jahre, 100 %, Vergütung nach TV-L E 13) in der von Prof. Dr. Alexander Martin geleiteten Analytics and Optimization Group an. Wir suchen eine hoch motivierte und qualifizierte Person zur Verstärkung unseres dynamischen und internationalen Forschungsteams. Die erfolgreiche Bewerberin bzw. der erfolgreiche Bewerber wird Teil eines interdisziplinären Forschungsteams, das neue Ansätze für Multi-Agent Path Finding in großen robotergestützten Lagersystemen entwickelt. Die Stelle ist im Bereich der mathematischen Optimierung angesiedelt und umfasst eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit Forschenden aus Robotik und Business Intelligence. Sie forschen unter anderem zu gemischt-ganzzahliger Optimierung für Multi-Agent Path Finding, Optimierung unter Unsicherheit und optimierungsbasierter Konfliktlösung und bringen Ihre Expertise in mathematischer Optimierung in das interdisziplinäre Team ein. Die entwickelten Methoden werden sowohl in Simulationen als auch auf realen Robotersystemen evaluiert. Eine komplementäre, im Bereich Robotik angesiedelte Promotionsstelle wird in der von Prof. Dr. Wolfram Burgard geleiteten Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Group ausgeschrieben. Weitere beteiligte Forschungsgruppen sind die von Dr. Tanja Kaiser geleitete Multi-Robot Systems Junior Research Group, die von Prof. Dr. Johannes Thürauf geleitete Discrete Optimization Group sowie die Management Intelligence Services Group der FAU unter der Leitung von Prof. Dr. Freimut Bodendorf. Ihre Aufgaben: Die erfolgreiche Bewerberin bzw. der erfolgreiche Bewerber wird im interdisziplinären Projekt „Real-World Multi-Agent Optimal Path Finding under Uncertainty“ mitwirken. Zu Ihren Aufgaben gehören: Durchführung innovativer Forschung zur mathematischen Optimierung für Multi-Agent Path Finding in enger Zusammenarbeit mit einem interdisziplinären Forschungsteam. Entwicklung mathematischer Optimierungsmethoden, insbesondere gemischt-ganzzahliger Optimierungsansätze, für die Pfadplanung von Multi-Agenten-Systemen und die Lösung komplexer Konflikte in realen Robotersystemen. Entwicklung von Optimierungsansätzen unter Unsicherheit, um zuverlässige Lösungen bei unsicherem Roboterverhalten, schwankender Nachfrage und variierenden Betriebsbedingungen zu erzielen. Implementierung und rechnergestützte Evaluation der entwickelten Optimierungsmethoden, einschließlich ihrer Erprobung auf realen Robotersystemen. Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Forschenden aus der Robotik sowie der Management Intelligence Services Group der FAU, um Optimierung, Robotik und Business Intelligence miteinander zu verbinden. Veröffentlichung von Forschungsergebnissen in führenden internationalen Fachzeitschriften und auf renommierten Konferenzen sowie Präsentation der eigenen Forschung auf internationalen Konferenzen. Mitwirkung in der Lehre und Betreuung von Studierenden, z. B. im Rahmen von Lehrveranstaltungen, Abschlussarbeiten und Forschungsprojekten. Mitwirkung an Outreach-Aktivitäten und Kommunikation von Forschungsergebnissen gegenüber Wissenschaft, Industrie und Öffentlichkeit. Ihr Profil: Wir erwarten: Einen qualifizierenden Hochschulabschluss (M.Sc. oder vergleichbar) in Mathematik, Informatik, Operations Research oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet, einschließlich Natur- und Ingenieurwissenschaften Motivation, Engagement und ein hohes Maß an Verantwortungsbewusstsein Solide mathematische Kenntnisse und ein ausgeprägtes Interesse an mathematischer Optimierung Ausgeprägtes Interesse an interdisziplinärer Forschung Programmiererfahrung, z. B. in Python, C++ oder vergleichbaren Programmiersprachen Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift Zusätzliche Kenntnisse oder Erfahrungen in einem oder mehreren der folgenden Bereiche sind wünschenswert: Gemischt-ganzzahlige Optimierung und mathematische Programmierung Optimierung unter Unsicherheit Optimierungssoftware, z. B. Gurobi, CPLEX oder SCIP Algorithmenentwicklung und rechnergestützte Optimierung Ausgewählte Vorteile dieser Position: Eine besondere Gelegenheit, an der Schnittstelle von mathematischer Optimierung, Robotik und Business Intelligence zu forschen, dabei fundierte Expertise in der Optimierung aufzubauen und eng mit verschiedenen Disziplinen zusammenzuarbeiten. Die Möglichkeit, neuartige mathematische Optimierungsmethoden zu entwickeln und diese an anspruchsvollen realen Multi-Roboter-Systemen zu evaluieren. Zugang zu umfassender Expertise über verschiedene Forschungsgruppen und Departments der UTN hinweg sowie zu leistungsfähigen Rechenressourcen. Attraktive Vergütung nach TV-L E 13 sowie eine hohe Lebensqualität bei vergleichsweise moderaten Lebenshaltungskosten in Nürnberg. Interessiert? Wenn Ihr Profil den Anforderungen entspricht, laden Sie bitte folgende Dokumente mit ihrer Bewerbung hoch: Ein Persönliches Motivationsschreiben (max. 1 Seite), in dem Sie die Gründe für Ihren Promotionswunsch an der UTN darlegen und weshalb Sie sich für dieses Forschungsfeld und das Department interessieren. Ein vollständiger chronologischer, tabellarischer Lebenslauf in englischer Sprache. Nachweise über Ihre Studienabschlüsse (M.Sc. sowie B.Sc.) oder gleichwertige Qualifikationen. Transcript of Records, Diploma Supplements oder Kursübersichten ihrer Studienabschlüsse (M.Sc. sowie B.Sc. oder gleichwertige Abschlüsse). Bitte beachten: Falls Sie Ihre Abschlüsse (M.Sc. sowie B.Sc. oder gleichwertige Abschlüsse) im Ausland erhalten haben, müssen Sie stets die Originalversion zusammen mit einer Übersetzung ins Englische oder Deutsche einreichen. Die Übersetzung muss von einem staatlich geprüften Übersetzer/einer staatlich geprüften Übersetzerin angefertigt worden sein und über ein offizielles Siegel verfügen. Dokumente, deren Originalsprache Englisch ist, müssen nicht übersetzt werden. Hinweise zum Motivationsschreiben: Wenn Ihr Motivationsschreiben überwiegend KI generiert erscheint, kann dies Ihre Chancen im weiteren Auswahlverfahren deutlich verringern. Wir möchten Ihre persönliche Motivation kennenlernen und verstehen, an welchen Themen Sie forschen möchten. Sollten Sie in die engere Auswahl kommen, erhalten Sie eine Einladung zu einem Interview, bei dem Sie Ihre Forschungsarbeit vorstellen können. Die Bewerbungen werden fortlaufend geprüft. Wir empfehlen daher eine frühzeitige Bewerbung. Bitte richten Sie alle inhaltlichen Anfragen Prof. Dr. Alexander Martin alexander.martin@utn.de Bei allgemeinen Fragen wenden Sie sich bitte an stars@utn.de The University of Technology Nuremberg (UTN) offers a stimulating and interdisciplinary research environment with access to cutting-edge resources. It is the ideal place to make groundbreaking discoveries and contribute to exciting fields of research. Doctoral researcher (Ph.D.) position at UTN with the topic of Mathematical Optimization for Multi-Robot Systems (m/f/d) The Department of Liberal Arts & Social Sciences is currently offering one opening for a doctoral research opportunity (fully funded, 3 years, 100%, pay scale TV-L E 13) in the Analytics and Optimization Group led by Prof. Dr. Alexander Martin. We are seeking a highly motivated and talented individual to join our dynamic and international research team. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team of researchers developing novel approaches to multi-agent path finding in large-scale robotic warehouses. The position is rooted in mathematical optimization and involves close collaboration with researchers in robotics and business intelligence. You will conduct research on topics such as mixed-integer optimization for multi-agent path finding, optimization under uncertainty, and optimization-based conflict resolution, and contribute mathematical optimization expertise to the interdisciplinary team. The developed methods will be evaluated in simulation and on real robotic systems. There will be a complementary position rooted in robotics available in the Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Group led by Prof. Dr. Wolfram Burgard. Further involved research groups are the Multi-Robot Systems Junior Research Group led by Dr. Tanja Kaiser, the Discrete Optimization Group led by Prof. Dr. Johannes Thürauf, and FAU’s Management Intelligence Services Group led by Prof. Dr. Freimut Bodendorf. Your tasks: The successful candidate will contribute to the interdisciplinary project “Real-World Multi-Agent Optimal Path Finding under Uncertainty”. Your responsibilities will include: Conducting cutting-edge research on mathematical optimization for multi-agent path finding in close collaboration with an interdisciplinary team. Developing mathematical optimization methods, such as mixed-integer optimization approaches, for multi-agent path planning and complex conflict resolution in real-world robotic systems. Developing optimization approaches under uncertainty to obtain reliable solutions under uncertain robot behavior, demand, and operating conditions. Implementing and computationally evaluating the developed optimization methods, including their evaluation in real-world robotic systems. Closely collaborating with researchers in robotics and FAU’s Management Intelligence Services Group to integrate optimization, robotics, and business intelligence. Publishing research results in leading international journals and conferences and presenting your work to the global research community at international conferences. Contributing to teaching activities and student supervision (e.g., courses, theses, research projects). Engaging in outreach activities and communicating research to academic, industrial, and wider public audiences. Your profile: We expect: A qualifying degree (M.Sc. or equivalent) in Mathematics, Computer Science, Operations Research, or a related discipline including natural sciences and engineering Motivation, dedication, and a strong sense of responsibility A solid mathematical background and strong interest in mathematical optimization Strong interest in interdisciplinary research Programming experience, e.g., Python, C++, or related languages Proficiency in English (spoken and written) Additional experience in one or more of the following areas is desirable: Mixed-integer optimization and mathematical programming Optimization under uncertainty Optimization software (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP) Algorithm development and computational optimization Selected highlights of this position include: A unique opportunity to conduct research at the intersection of mathematical optimization, robotics, and business intelligence, while developing deep expertise in optimization and collaborating closely across disciplines. The opportunity to develop novel mathematical optimization methods and evaluate them on challenging real-world multi-robot systems. Access to broad expertise across UTN’s groups and departments, as well as computational resources. Competitive compensation according to TVL E 13, together with the high quality of living and comparatively moderate living costs offered by the city of Nuremberg. Interested? items.title: Doctorante / Doctorant CIFRE Fiabilité des jumeaux numériques dans le ferroviaire
items.desc: Description De L'employeur Le Groupe SNCF a pour vocation de simplifier les déplacements, fluidifier le transport des personnes et des marchandises, et développer la mobilité de demain. Au sein du Groupe SNCF, la Direction Technologies, Innovation et Projets Groupe (DTIPG) est une direction de la SA SNCF chargée de l'innovation technologique appliquée aux projets stratégiques du groupe. Elle contribue notamment à concevoir un système ferroviaire plus fiable, numérique et décarboné, avec des travaux sur l'IA, les nouvelles propulsions et la localisation des trains. Dans ce cadre, le pôle RECHERCHE - DIRECTION SCIENTIFIQUE propose un projet de thèse CIFRE sur la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques dans le ferroviaire , en partenariat avec le Laboratoire en Génie Industriel (LGI) de CentraleSupélec au sein de la chaire Risques et Résilience des Systèmes Complexes (RRSC) . Description Du Poste La doctorante ou le doctorant CIFRE aura pour mission de développer une méthode d'évaluation et de communication de la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques (JN) appliqués aux systèmes ferroviaires. Les principales activités seront : Comprendre et formaliser les usages des jumeaux numériques dans le ferroviaire : Analyse des cas d'usage SNCF et partenaires (conception numérique, supervision du patrimoine, planification de la maintenance, régénération du réseau). Cartographie des composants d'un JN (données, modèles sous-jacents, processus, interfaces). Réaliser un état de l'art approfondi : Revue bibliographique sur les concepts de jumeaux numériques, la qualité des données et des modèles, la confiance et la fiabilité perçue par les utilisateurs. Analyse des normes et référentiels (notamment ISO/IEC 30173:2023 et ISO 23247:2021) et des modèles de maturité (Digital Twin Business Maturity Model). Cartographier et classifier les cas d'usage SNCF : Identification des étapes de conception d'un JN et de ses niveaux de maturité. Recueil des usages métiers (par qui, pour quoi) et des limites identifiées. Analyse de la fiabilité perçue : critères utilisés, justifications, attentes des utilisateurs. Méthodes : entretiens, analyse documentaire, enquêtes auprès des équipes SNCF et des partenaires. Étudier en profondeur un ou plusieurs cas d'étude : Définition du processus complet de conception et d'utilisation d'un JN sur un cas choisi (par exemple un système de signalisation ou un sous-système d'infrastructure). Identification des étapes où interviennent les contraintes de fiabilité (collecte des données, modélisation, prédiction, décision). Modélisation du processus de conception et d'usage du JN. Méthodes : entretiens, analyse de données, modélisation de processus. Proposer une méthode de notation de la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques : Analyse des enjeux : pour qui, pourquoi et à quoi sert la notation (support à la décision, communication, gouvernance). Définition des dimensions d'évaluation de la fiabilité, éventuellement différenciées selon les types de JN (descriptif, diagnostique, prédictif, prescriptif, autonome). Choix et formalisation d'une méthodologie de notation (par exemple analyse multicritère, indicateurs composites inspirés de modèles type « nutri-score » adaptés aux JN). Expérimentation et test de la méthode sur un ou plusieurs cas d'étude ferroviaire. Conception participative avec des experts métiers et techniques SNCF. Inscrire les travaux dans un écosystème européen : Veille et participation aux travaux autour des jumeaux numériques ferroviaires dans le projet Motional du programme Europes'Rail, et le cas échéant Motional 2. Valorisation des résultats de la thèse auprès des partenaires européens (présentations, publications, contributions aux groupes de travail). Production scientifique et valorisation : Rédaction d'articles scientifiques, rapports internes SNCF, supports de vulgarisation pour les métiers. Participation à des conférences et séminaires (académiques et industriels). Profil recherché Diplômé(e) de Master 2 ou école d'ingénieur Dans Un Des Domaines Suivants (ou Apparentés) Génie industriel Modélisation et simulation de systèmes complexes Ingénierie des systèmes Mathématiques appliquées / data science avec forte appétence pour les systèmes industriels Ou formation équivalente avec solide bagage en modélisation et analyse de systèmes. Un intérêt marqué pour le système ferroviaire , ses enjeux techniques et humains, est attendu. Compétences techniques Solide maîtrise de la modélisation et de la simulation de systèmes complexes (approches systèmes, modèles de processus, éventuellement outils de modélisation type UML, SysML ou équivalents). Connaissances en ingénierie des systèmes et/ou génie industriel. Capacité à mener un état de l'art scientifique : recherche bibliographique, analyse critique d'articles, synthèse. Aisance avec les méthodes d'analyse multicritère et d'évaluation (indicateurs, agrégation, notation). Compétences en analyse de données et compréhension des enjeux de qualité des données (détection d'anomalies, données aberrantes, capteurs IoT...). Excellentes capacités de rédaction en français et en anglais (articles, rapports, documents méthodologiques). Compétences comportementales Capacité d'écoute et de dialogue avec des interlocuteurs variés (experts techniques, chercheurs, opérationnels métiers). Rigueur scientifique, sens de l'analyse et de la synthèse. Très bon relationnel et aptitude à travailler en interface entre monde académique et industriel. Autonomie, curiosité, goût pour l'innovation et la transformation numérique. Capacité à vulgariser des concepts complexes pour les rendre accessibles aux décideurs et aux utilisateurs métiers. Ce que le contrat CIFRE vous apportera Une expérience de recherche appliquée au coeur des enjeux de transformation numérique du ferroviaire : vous travaillerez sur un sujet stratégique pour SNCF et ses partenaires, à l'interface entre innovation digitale, systèmes complexes et performance du réseau. Une double immersion académique et industrielle : Au LGI de CentraleSupélec, au sein de la chaire RRSC, dans un environnement scientifique de haut niveau. Au sein de SNCF Holding - Direction Technologies, Innovation & Projets Groupe, en lien direct avec des experts du jumeau numérique, de la donnée et des systèmes ferroviaires. Un sujet fortement valorisable : Production d'une méthode de référence pour évaluer la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques ferroviaires. Contributions possibles à des projets européens (Motional, Europes'Rail) et à des groupes de normalisation ou de standardisation. Des perspectives professionnelles solides : Expertise rare et recherchée sur les jumeaux numériques, la fiabilité et la confiance dans les systèmes digitaux. Profil attractif pour le secteur ferroviaire, la mobilité, l'industrie et la tech (ingénierie systèmes, data, R&D, innovation). Rejoignez-nous et postulez en ligne dès maintenant en déposant votre CV accompagné d'une lettre de motivation

items.title: PhD In Developing Multi-Intelligence Agents For Evolving Cyber-Physical-Social Systems
items.desc: About the opportunity Join Cranfield University’s Systems Realization Group (SRG) for an MSc by Research exploring Evolving Cyber-Physical-Social Systems (eCPSS) . This project combines software engineering, data science and human-centred AI to integrate existing research demonstrators into a usable, client-facing decision-support platform. SRG develops and evaluates principles and mechanisms that help engineered systems adapt to changing requirements while preserving safety, accountable human authority and sustainability. Your research will support the translation of these advances into tools that organisations can evaluate and use. Success will involve delivering a working minimum viable product (MVP), documenting its architecture and evaluating how effectively it supports users in completing tasks, understanding recommendations and tracing decisions. Responsibilities Assess existing research demonstrators and identify their integration requirements. Develop a modular software architecture and shared data interfaces. Connect components through APIs or adapters. Build a web interface that enables users to explore operational changes, compare responses and review decision rationale. Retain appropriate human approval and record decisions throughout the workflow. Evaluate integration reliability, usability, task completion and decision traceability using agreed manufacturing scenarios. Collaborate with SRG researchers and demonstrator developers. Produce technical documentation, reproducible installation guidance and an MSc by Research thesis. Qualifications A first- or second-class UK honours degree, or equivalent, in Computer Science or Data Science. Related computing disciplines with equivalent practical experience may also be considered. Strong programming skills in Python or an equivalent language, with evidence of building working software. Ability to work with APIs, structured data, databases and version control. Experience developing user-facing applications. Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively. An interest in human-centred design, accountable AI and applied research. Experience with JavaScript/TypeScript, web frameworks, automated testing, AI/LLM integration, knowledge graphs or software deployment is desirable. Prior manufacturing or healthcare experience is not required. Applicants are encouraged to share relevant projects or a portfolio/repository link. Study arrangements This is a self-funded MSc by Research opportunity , rather than a salaried position. The duration is one year full-time or two years part-time , and applications are welcome from UK and international candidates. For enquiries, contact Dr Jelena Milisavljevic Syed at jelenams@cranfield.ac.uk. View the opportunity and apply

items.title: Doktorand i atmosfärsvetenskap och oceanografi, med fokus på ML-metoder i klimatmodellering
items.desc: Meteorologiska institutionen vid Stockholms universitet (MISU) bedriver forskning och utbildning som rör atmosfären, oceanen, och fysikaliskt-baserad klimatvetenskap. MISU erbjuder utbildningsprogram på kandidat-, master- och forskarnivå. Vår forskning söker svar på grundläggande frågor om atmosfärens och havens dynamiska, fysiska, kemiska, och biogeokemiska egenskaper av relevans för väder och klimat. Vi strävar efter en bred forskningsverksamhet inom vårt vetenskapliga område. Vi studerar frågor som sträcker sig från djuphavet till den övre atmosfären och från tropikerna till polerna. I vår forskning utnyttjar och utvecklar vi teori, statistiska metoder och numeriska modeller i nära samspel med observationer. Dessutom utvecklar och leder institutionen observationsbaserad forskning med stöd av satelliter, arktiska isbrytarexpeditioner och landbaserade instrument. MISU har cirka 60 anställda och ingår i en större forskningsmiljö som inkluderar Bolincentret för klimatforskning, Östersjöcentrum och Swedish e-Science Research Centre. Institutionen har stark internationell prägel, över hälften av medarbetarna har en bakgrund utanför Sverige och både svenska och engelska används som arbetsspråk. Vi välkomnar och värdesätter mångfald i vår arbetsmiljö. Mer information om oss finns på: Meteorologiska institutionen. Projektbeskrivning Moln och deras förändringar till följd av variationer i omgivande miljö spelar en avgörande för klimat och klimatförändringar. Upplösningen i typiska klimatmodeller är dock alldeles för grov för att de ska kunna representera processer relaterade till molnbildning explicit. Dessa processer behöver därför parametriseras, eller representeras som funktioner av storskaliga tillståndsvariabler. Sådana parametriseringar är behäftade med stor osäkerhet, och dessutom är de beräkningsmässigt kostsamma. Det här projektets fokus är att på nya sätt brygga över mellan mikroskala och global skala, för att förbättra klimatmodellers noggrannhet, effektivitet och generaliserbarhet och samtidigt utnyttja modern beräkningshårdvara. Vi kommer att undersöka hur maskininlärningsmodeller (ML-modeller) kan tränas på observationer och resultat från högupplöst modellering, som alternativ till empiriska parmetriseringar av småskaliga processer relaterade till turbulens, molnbildning och aerosol-moln-interaktioner. Specifikt ingår i uppgifterna att utveckla och träna datadrivna modeller, koppla dem till en storskalig klimatmodell, utvärdera resultaten mot mätningar och traditionellt parametriserade modeller, och att använda den ML-förstärkta modellen till att uppskatta klimatrelevans som molns effekt på strålningsbalansen, och strålningsdrivning från aerosol-moln-interaktioner. Arbetet kommer att utföras i nära samarbete med experter inom datavetenskap, inom Swedish e-Science Research Centre, och bidra till metodutveckling med bredare tillämpning än endast klimatvetenskap. Som doktorand i projektet kommer du att utveckla dina färdigheter inom atmosfärsvetenskap och klimatmodellering, men även inom datavetenskap och maskininlärning, samt kommunikation och samarbete inom och mellan discipliner. Behörighetskrav För att bli antagen till forskarutbildning krävs att den sökande har grundläggande och särskild behörighet. Behörigheten ska vara uppfylld senast vid antagning till programmet. Grundläggande behörighet har du, om du avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng (hp), varav minst 60 hp på avancerad nivå, eller på annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. För särskild behörighet krävs minst 90 hp i något av ämnena meteorologi, oceanografi, fysik eller kemi, minst 15 hp i matematik och ett självständigt arbete om minst 15 hp. Av detta skall minst 60 hp vara på avancerad nivå. Vidare krävs språkkunskaper i engelska motsvarande engelska B på gymnasiet. Allmän studieplan för utbildning på forskarnivå i atmosfärsvetenskap och oceanografi. Urval Urval bland de sökande som uppfyller behörighetskraven ska göras med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig utbildningen. Enbart det förhållandet att en sökande bedöms kunna få tidigare utbildning eller yrkesverksamhet tillgodoräknad för utbildningen får inte vid urval ge sökanden företräde framför andra sökande. Beslut om antagning fattas enligt gällande delegationsordning. Vid bedömningen tas hänsyn till förtrogenhet och skicklighet inom ämnet, förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på engelska, analytisk förmåga, kreativitet, initiativförmåga och självständighet, och samarbetsförmåga. Till grund för bedömningen ligger tidigare studiers relevans, betyg på genomgångna högskolekurser (särskilt de på avancerad nivå), kvalitet och omfattning på det självständiga arbetet, referenser, intervjuer samt skriftlig avsiktsförklaring. Antagningsordning för utbildning på forskarnivå vid Stockholms universitet. Om anställningen Tillträde enligt överenskommelse. Vi erbjuder en tidsbegränsad anställning som doktorand enligt 5 kap. högskoleförordningen (1993:100). Anställningstiden får inte vara längre än vad som motsvarar utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid under fyra år. Som doktorand ska du främst ägna dig åt din egen utbildning på forskarnivå, men i anställningen kan arbete med utbildning, forskning och administration ingå i begränsad omfattning (högst 20 %). En ny anställning som doktorand gäller för högst ett år, anställningen förnyas därefter med högst två år i taget. Stockholms universitet värnar om att vara en arbetsplats som är fri från diskriminering och ger lika rättigheter och möjligheter för alla. Kontakt För mer information om projektet, kontakta professor Frida Bender, frida.bender@misu.su.se. För information om forskarutbildningen, kontakta studierektor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. Upplysningar om rekryteringsprocessen och anställningsvillkor lämnas av administrativ chef, Sara Engström sara.engstrom@misu.su.se. Ansökan Du söker doktorandplatsen via Stockholms universitets rekryteringssystem. Bifoga personligt brev och CV samt de bilagor som efterfrågas i ansökningsformuläret. Du som sökande ansvarar för att ansökan är komplett i enlighet med annonsen och att den är universitetet tillhanda senast sista ansökningsdag. Vi ber att du som sökande avstår från att skicka in en AI-genererad ansökan. Anvisningar för sökande finns på webbsidan: att söka en anställning. Stockholms universitet bidrar till det hållbara demokratiska samhällets utveckling genom kunskap, upplysning och sanningssökande.
