items.co: ISAE-Supméca – Institut supérieur de mécanique de Paris
items.title: Offre de thèse CIFRE Janvier/Février 2027
items.desc: Pérennisation soutenable des systèmes de production : modélisation probabiliste hybride et anticipation des risques d’obsolescence Contexte et problématique Une part importante de l’outil industriel repose aujourd’hui sur des installations exploitées depuis plusieurs décennies. Ces moyens de production associent des équipements, composants, automatismes et logiciels dont la durée d’exploitation dépasse fréquemment celle de commercialisation ou de support. L’obsolescence constitue ainsi un risque important pour la continuité de production. Elle peut résulter d’évolutions technologiques, de l’arrêt d’une référence, de la raréfaction de pièces, de la disparition d’un fournisseur, de la fin d’un support ou de la perte de compétences. Sa maîtrise constitue un enjeu de disponibilité des installations, de souveraineté industrielle et d’utilisation raisonnée des ressources. Une installation industrielle comporte plusieurs milliers de références reliées entre elles au sein d’architectures techniques et de chaînes d’approvisionnement complexes. Les informations nécessaires à l’évaluation de leur pérennité sont dispersées entre bases de maintenance, référentiels techniques, données fournisseurs, historiques d’intervention et connaissances métier. Ces informations sont hétérogènes, évolutives et souvent incomplètes. Le module de diagnostic du logiciel OBSOLIO, développé par GreenTrack Genius, évalue actuellement l’obsolescence au moyen d’un scoring expert statique. La thèse vise à dépasser cette approche pour construire un modèle capable d’actualiser et d’anticiper le risque d’obsolescence à partir des données disponibles et des connaissances métier, tout en représentant explicitement l’incertitude et les mécanismes de propagation du risque. Question scientifique centrale Comment modéliser, propager et actualiser le risque d’obsolescence au sein d’une architecture industrielle multiniveau et de sa chaîne d’approvisionnement, en présence d’informations hétérogènes et incomplètes, afin de comparer de manière explicable des stratégies de pérennisation soutenable ? Verrou scientifique et approche proposée Le principal verrou scientifique concerne la propagation probabiliste d’un risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau, depuis le composant jusqu’à l’équipement et à la ligne de production, alors que l’état de connaissance sur les différents éléments du système est incomplet et variable. Une absence d’information sur une référence, un fournisseur ou une possibilité de substitution ne peut en effet être assimilée à l’absence de risque, ni être systématiquement considérée comme une situation défavorable. La modélisation devra donc distinguer autant que possible le risque déduit des informations disponibles de l’incertitude liée à l’incomplétude de ces informations. La recherche s’appuiera sur une approche hybride associant deux niveaux de représentation. 1. Représentation des connaissances et de l’architecture industrielle Un graphe de connaissances sera utilisé pour structurer les relations entre actifs, composants, nomenclatures, fournisseurs, références de substitution, historiques et événements d’obsolescence. Ce graphe aura pour fonction de représenter la structure du système étudié et les informations disponibles. Une question de recherche portera sur la manière de transformer ou d’exploiter cette représentation pour construire les dépendances pertinentes du modèle probabiliste. 2. Modélisation et propagation probabilistes Les réseaux bayésiens constitueront le cadre principal étudié pour agréger les connaissances expertes et les observations disponibles, représenter les dépendances entre facteurs et propager l’incertitude entre les différents niveaux du système. La dimension temporelle sera introduite lorsque les données disponibles permettent de caractériser l’évolution des variables et du risque. Les extensions dynamiques des réseaux bayésiens seront notamment étudiées pour représenter cette évolution et évaluer leur capacité à anticiper une situation d’obsolescence. Le travail portera en particulier sur les méthodes d’initialisation du modèle, l’intégration de connaissances expertes, l’apprentissage à partir des historiques et la robustesse de l’inférence en présence de données manquantes. Aide à la décision et pérennisation soutenable L’objectif est de dépasser le diagnostic pour comparer des stratégies de remédiation. Les réseaux bayésiens pourront être étendus sous forme de diagrammes d’influence, intégrant variables de décision et critères d’utilité. Plusieurs stratégies seront considérées : maintien en l’état, constitution ou mutualisation de stocks, substitution, reconditionnement, reconception partielle ou renouvellement. La pérennisation soutenable sera abordée comme un problème de décision multicritère prenant en compte au minimum : la disponibilité et le risque technique ; le coût de la stratégie ; son impact environnemental ; sa faisabilité industrielle et organisationnelle. L’objectif sera donc d’identifier la solution réduisant le risque d’obsolescence mais aussi de comparer les conséquences de différentes stratégies dans le contexte propre au système étudié. Validation et résultats attendus La validation reposera sur des données industrielles historiques : données de maintenance et d’équipements, informations fournisseurs, changements de références, événements d’obsolescence et autres données de cycle de vie disponibles sur les sites étudiés. Une validation rétrospective sera privilégiée. Elle consistera, lorsque les données le permettent, à reconstruire l’état d’information disponible à une date passée, à produire l’évaluation du risque correspondant, puis à comparer cette évaluation aux événements observés ultérieurement. Les résultats seront également comparés au scoring expert actuellement utilisé dans OBSOLIO afin de mesurer l’apport de la modélisation probabiliste en matière d’anticipation, de gestion des données manquantes et d’explicabilité. La thèse devra aboutir à trois résultats principaux : un modèle formel de représentation et de propagation probabiliste du risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau ; une méthode d’aide à la décision permettant de comparer des stratégies de pérennisation selon plusieurs critères ; un démonstrateur Python mettant en œuvre les modèles développés et permettant leur validation sur des cas industriels. Les contributions scientifiques porteront ainsi sur la représentation et la propagation d’un risque d’obsolescence dans des systèmes industriels complexes lorsque l’information disponible est distribuée, évolutive et incomplète. Les résultats auront vocation à alimenter le moteur algorithmique d’OBSOLIO, sans que le développement du logiciel constitue l’objet de la thèse. Profil recherché Le ou la candidate devra être titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master en génie industriel, ingénierie des systèmes, science des données, informatique industrielle ou domaine proche. De solides bases en probabilités, statistiques et modélisation sont attendues, ainsi qu’une bonne maîtrise de la programmation scientifique en Python. Une connaissance des réseaux bayésiens, des modèles graphiques probabilistes ou des méthodes de recherche opérationnelle constituera un atout. Le travail nécessitera également une capacité à comprendre des architectures industrielles complexes et à travailler avec les équipes de maintenance, méthodes, achats et ingénierie. Le profil recherché doit ainsi associer compétences en modélisation et intérêt pour les problématiques industrielles concrètes. Contact : Marc.Zolghadri@isae-supmeca.fr

items.title: Ph.D. Cadidate (m/f/d)
items.desc: Job description: Ph.D. Cadidate (m/f/d) at the Institute for Medical Informatics and Biometry The position is to be filled as soon as possible on a full-time or part-time basis for a fixed term of 36 months. Remuneration is based on the classification provisions of the Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the Federal States (TV-L); placement in pay group E13 is possible, subject to the fulfillment of personal requirements. The Institute for Medical Informatics and Biometry (IMB) is part of the Carl Gustav Carus Faculty of Medicine at TU Dresden. The institute’s research focuses on medical biometrics, bioinformatics, systems biology/medicine, including mathematical modelling, as well as medical informatics. In addition to these scientific activities, the IMB offers various services (e.g., consulting and education programs in the field of medical data science) for faculty and students at the Faculty of Medicine and the University Hospital. The position is part of the interdisciplinary research project “Virtual niche: Computational modelling and simulation of spatio-temporal dynamics of hematopoietic stem cells in their local microenvironment” funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). The core objective of the project is the development and application of a mathematical model that describes the spatio-temporal organization of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in their local growth environment within the bone marrow. The goal of gaining a better understanding of the underlying processes is of central importance both for open questions in basic stem cell biology and for future medical applications. Your responsibilities: Development of mathematical models to describe cellular dynamics Implementation of the models in a suitable programming environment Simulation of cellular dynamics within complex 3D structures Application of the computer model as a virtual bridge between in vitro and in vivo studies Systemic analysis and interpretation of experimental data in the context of complex biological interactions Close interdisciplinary collaboration with experimental teams at TU Dresden and external partner laboratories Your Profil: University degree (M.Sc., Diplom, or equivalent) in mathematics, physics, computer science, engineering (with biological/biotechnological focus) or a related field Very good or excellent academic record Strong interest in interdisciplinary work, particularly in the application of mathematical and computational methods in biology and medicine Solid programming experience (e.g. in the statistical software R or Python) Knowledge of (stem) cell biology and experience in mathematical modelling are advantageous Reliability, creativity, flexibility, and the ability to work well in a team A cooperative, self-motivated, and goal-oriented work style Very good English skills We offer: Compensation: Based on the TV-L Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the Federal States in pay grade E13 , plus an annual bonus, provided you meet the personal requirements Vacation: 30 days of paid vacation Professional Development: Extensive internal and external training and development opportunities to continuously strengthen your skills Company Culture: We value transparency, team spirit, and shared success. Celebrate with us at company gatherings or sporting events like the Rewe Team Challenge. Mobility: A subsidy for a job ticket to make your commute eco-friendly and convenient Health: We promote your well-being with modern fitness and exercise programs at our health center, mental health programs, and a comprehensive workplace health management program. Shopping benefits: Take advantage of employee discounts at our clinic pharmacy, exclusive corporate benefits, and other shopping portals. Work-life balance: Our Family Office supports you with questions regarding daycare spots, vacation programs, and caring for family members. We also offer flexible work arrangements. For preliminary information, please contact Prof. Dr. Ingo Roeder by phone at 0351-458-6060 or by email at ingo.roeder@tu-dresden.de (Subject: DFG-virtualniche)

items.title: Doktorandin/Doktorand (m/w/d) AG Röder
items.desc: Stellenbeschreibung: Doktorandin/Doktorand (m/w/d) am Institut für Medizinische Informatik und Biometrie Die Stelle ist zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt in Voll- oder Teilzeitbeschäftigung für 36 Monate befristet zu besetzen. Die Vergütung erfolgt nach den Eingruppierungsvorschriften des Tarifvertrages für den öffentlichen Dienst (TV-L) und ist bei Vorliegen der persönlichen Voraussetzungen in die Entgeltgruppe E13 möglich. Das Institut für Medizinische Informatik und Biometrie (IMB) ist Teil der Medizinischen Fakultät Carl Gustav Carus der Technischen Universität Dresden. Die Forschungsschwerpunkte des Instituts liegen in den Bereichen medizinische Biometrie, Bioinformatik, Systembiologie/-medizin inklusive der mathematischen Modellierung sowie in der medizinischen Informatik. Neben diesen wissenschaftlichen Tätigkeitsfeldern bietet das IMB verschiedene Dienstleistungen (z. B. Beratungs- und Weiterbildungsangebote im Bereich der medizinischen Datenwissenschaften) für Mitarbeitende und Studierende der Medizinischen Fakultät und des Universitätsklinikums Dresden an. Die Stelle ist Teil des von der Deutschen Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) geförderten interdisziplinären Forschungsprojekts „Virtuelle Nische: Computer-gestützte Modellierung und Simulation der zeitlichen-räumlich Dynamik hämatopoetischer Stammzellen in ihrer lokalen Mikroumgebung“. Kernziel des Projektes ist die Entwicklung und Anwendung eines mathematischen Modells, das die zeitlich‑räumliche Organisation hämatopoetischer Stamm‑ und Vorläuferzellen in ihrer lokalen Wachstumsumgebung im Knochenmark beschreibt. Das angestrebte verbesserte Verständnis der zugrundeliegenden Prozesse ist sowohl für offene grundlagenwissenschaftliche Fragestellungen der Stammzellbiologie als auch für zukünftige medizinische Anwendungen von zentraler Bedeutung. Ihre Aufgaben: Entwicklung mathematischer Modelle zur Beschreibung zellulärer Dynamiken Implementierung der Modelle in einer geeigneten Programmierumgebung Simulation zellulärer Dynamiken innerhalb komplexer 3D-Strukturen Anwendung des Computermodells als virtuelle Brücke zwischen in vitro- und in vivo-Studien Systemische Analyse und Interpretation experimenteller Daten im Kontext komplexer biologischer Interaktionen Enge interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit mit experimentell arbeitenden Teams an der TU Dresden und kooperierenden Laboren im europäischen Ausland Ihr Profil: abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (M.Sc., Diplom oder Vergleichbares) im Fach Mathematik, Physik, Informatik, Ingenieurwissenschaften (mit biologischem/technologischem Schwerpunkt) oder einer verwandten Disziplin sehr gute oder exzellente Studienleistungen ausgeprägtes Interesse an interdisziplinären Aufgaben, speziell an der Anwendung mathematischer/informatischer Methoden in der Biologie/Medizin solide Programmiererfahrung (z. B. in der Statistiksoftware R oder Python) Kenntnisse im Bereich (Stamm-)Zellbiologie und Erfahrungen im Bereich der mathematischen Modellierung sind vorteilhaft Zuverlässigkeit, Kreativität, Flexibilität und Teamfähigkeit kooperativer, eigenverantwortlicher und zielorientierter Arbeitsstil sehr gute Englischkenntnisse Unser Angebot: Vergütung: nach TV-L in der Entgeltgruppe E13 zzgl. Jahressonderzahlung, bei Vorliegen der persönlichen Voraussetzungen Urlaub: 30 Tage Erholungsurlaub Weiterbildung: Umfangreiche interne und externe Fort- und Weiterbildungsangebote, um Ihre Kompetenzen kontinuierlich zu stärken Unternehmenskultur : Wir setzen auf Transparenz, Teamgeist und gemeinsame Erfolge. Feiern Sie mit uns bei gemeinsamen Veranstaltungen oder bei sportlichen Events. Mobilität: Zuschuss zum Jobticket, um Ihren Arbeitsweg umweltfreundlich und bequem zu gestalten Gesundheit: Wir fördern Ihr Wohlbefinden mit modernen Sport- und Bewegungsangeboten in unserem Gesundheitszentrum, Programmen zur mentalen Gesundheit und einem umfassenden betrieblichen Gesundheitsmanagement. Einkaufsvorteile : Profitieren Sie von Mitarbeiterrabatten in unserer Klinik-Apotheke, exklusiven Corporate Benefits und weiteren Shoppingportalen. Work-Life-Balance: Unser Familienbüro unterstützt Sie bei Fragen rund um Kita-Plätze, Ferienprogramme und Pflege von Angehörigen. Zudem bieten wir flexible Arbeitsmodelle. Vorabinformationen erhalten Sie telefonisch von Herrn Prof. Dr. Ingo Röder unter 0351-458-6060 oder per E-Mail: ingo.roeder@tu-dresden.de (Betreff: DFG-virtualniche)

items.title: Promovendus digi-, data- en AI-competenties
items.desc: De zorg van morgen wordt steeds digitaler. Maar technologie werkt pas als zorgprofessionals ermee kunnen werken. Hoe leren studenten en professionals digi-, data- en AI-competenties? En hoe bereiden we hen voor op een snel veranderende digitale wereld? Dat onderzoek jij! Aantal uur: 28 • 36 uur per week Werklocatie: Beide locaties Amsterdam UMC Contractvorm: Bepaalde tijd Salaris: € 3.217 - € 4.077 Reageer tot en met: 2 november 2026 Wat ga je doen? Je combineert literatuuronderzoek met het ontwikkelen en evalueren van leertrajecten voor (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Je werkzaamheden bestaan uit: Je brengt de wetenschappelijke literatuur en de meest recente inzichten op het gebied van digi-, data- en AI-competenties en leren en ontwikkelen in kaart. Je schrijft een algemeen onderzoeksplan en werkt dit uit in deelstudies, inclusief de benodigde ethische goedkeuringen. Je onderzoekt modellen, methoden en technieken voor een leven lang ontwikkelen. Daarbij kijk je bijvoorbeeld naar transfer of training, simulatieleren en werkplekleren om tot schaalbare oplossingen te komen. Je ontwikkelt en evalueert leertrajecten, waaronder pilots, voor (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Je adviseert waar nodig projecten en programma's binnen Amsterdam UMC die aansluiten bij jouw onderzoek. Daarnaast schrijf je wetenschappelijke artikelen voor nationale en internationale tijdschriften. Je bundelt je onderzoeksresultaten uiteindelijk in een proefschrift en presenteert je bevindingen op nationale en internationale congressen. Ook draag je beperkt bij aan onderwijs en opleiden van studenten en medewerkers, voor zover dit aansluit bij jouw onderzoek. Wat neem je mee? We nodigen je uit om te solliciteren als je een van de volgende opleidingen hebt afgerond: Een (research)master onderwijskunde, met affiniteit met en bij voorkeur ervaring in de gezondheidszorg. Of: Een (research)master gezondheidswetenschappen, aangevuld met aantoonbare didactische ervaring of scholing. Daarnaast herken je jezelf in het volgende profiel: Je hebt aantoonbare affiniteit met onderzoek en ervaring met kwalitatieve en kwantitatieve onderzoeksmethoden. Je hebt interesse in digitalisering, data en AI in de zorg en in didactische principes zoals simulatieleren en werkplekleren, of je wilt je hierin verder verdiepen. Je bent analytisch sterk, zelfstandig en nieuwsgierig. Ook heb je het doorzettingsvermogen om een promotietraject succesvol af te ronden. Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels goed, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Je kunt complexe onderwerpen helder uitleggen. Ervaring met lesgeven of begeleiden is een pré. Je werkt graag samen, maar kunt ook zelfstandig aan de slag. Wat bieden we jou? Je treedt in dienst bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Een contract voor de duur van 12 maanden, met de intentie te verlengen tot een totaal van vier jaar. Voor deze vacature geldt de Richtlijn Promovendi. Inschaling in salarisschaal OIO: € 3.217 tot € 4.077 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Daarnaast ontvang je 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering. Bereken hier jouw netto salaris. Mogelijkheid tot hybride werken, waarbij je minimaal twee dagen per week op locatie werkt. Vakantie-uren: 194,4 uur per jaar bij een fulltime dienstverband en de mogelijkheid om uren bij te sparen. 100% OV-vergoeding. Kom je lopend, fietsend of met de auto? Dan ontvang je een vergoeding van €0,21 per km (voor de auto geldt een maximum van 40 km enkele reis). Kom je op de fiets? Maak gebruik van onze goede fietsregeling. Pensioenopbouw bij BeFrank, een modern, begrijpelijk en eerlijk geprijsd pensioen. Bekijk deze video met meer informatie over de indiensttreding bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Waar ga je werken ? Je werkt bij het Teaching & Learning Centre (TLC) van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de UvA, bij Amsterdam UMC, locatie AMC, aan de Meibergdreef. Je maakt deel uit van het onderzoeksteam, een van de vier teams binnen het TLC. Dit kleine team bestaat uit onderwijskundig onderzoekers en innovators die samenwerken aan onderwijsvernieuwing en onderzoek. Daarnaast werk je inhoudelijk samen met het projectteam dat de leerpaden voor digi-, data- en AI-vaardigheden binnen Amsterdam UMC ontwikkelt en in de praktijk brengt. Het TLC is het expertisecentrum voor hoger onderwijs van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de UvA. Het ondersteunt de opleidingen Geneeskunde en Medische informatiekunde bij het verzorgen van hoogwaardig onderwijs. Onderwijskundig adviseurs, medical educators, trainers, onderzoekers en innovators werken er samen aan het verbeteren van onderwijs en opleiden. Het TLC maakt deel uit van de kerntaak Onderwijs & Opleiden van Amsterdam UMC en draagt bij aan de ontwikkeling van studenten en (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Binnen het team heerst een open en samenwerkingsgerichte cultuur. Kennis delen en samen leren staan centraal. Je werkt ook nauw samen met onderzoekers van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de VU en met andere afdelingen binnen Amsterdam UMC. Zo draag je bij aan een groeiende community op het gebied van onderwijsonderzoek. Wat ga je onderzoeken? Je onderzoekt welke digi-, data- en AI-competenties huidige en toekomstige zorgprofessionals nodig hebben. Je brengt in kaart welke competenties al goed zijn ontwikkeld en waar nog hiaten of overlap bestaan. Op basis daarvan ontwikkel je een breed, evidence-based competentieraamwerk. Je doet voorstellen om deze competenties efficiënt te integreren in het continuüm van onderwijs en opleiden. Waar mogelijk evalueer je bestaande en nieuwe leerinterventies die aansluiten op (onderdelen van) het raamwerk. Daarbij kijk je niet alleen naar het directe leerrendement, maar ook naar de vraag of professionals de competenties op langere termijn behouden en toepassen. Je onderzoek sluit aan bij een groter project binnen Amsterdam UMC. Daarin ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en testen we al enkele jaren leerpaden voor verschillende doelgroepen. De ontwikkelde producten, zoals de ontwerpmethodiek, het eerste competentiemodel en het evaluatieproces, vormen de basis voor jouw onderzoek. Tegelijkertijd biedt deze context volop ruimte om nieuwe onderzoeksvragen te verkennen. Wil je alvast meer weten over de verschillende fases binnen het PhD-traject? Op deze pagina lees je hierover meer informatie. Laten we kennismaken De beoogde startdatum is zo snel mogelijk, in overleg. Heb je interesse? Stuur dan je motivatiebrief en cv, aangevuld met een publicatielijst indien relevant. De eerste ronde sollicitatiegesprekken vindt plaats in de week van maandag 16 november 2026 . Tijdens deze gesprekken maak je kennis met de vice-decaan Onderwijs van de UvA, het hoofd van het TLC en de coördinerend onderzoeker van het onderzoeksteam. We vragen je om hier alvast rekening mee te houden. Heb je nog vragen? Voor inhoudelijke informatie over deze vacature kun je terecht bij Tom Broens , h oofd TLC, via t.h.broens@amsterdamumc.nl . Een referentiecheck en screening kunnen onderdeel zijn van de procedure. Lees hier wat dit inhoudt. Kom je bij ons in dienst, dan vragen we een VOG (Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag). Interne kandidaten krijgen, bij gelijke geschiktheid, voorrang op externe kandidaten. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

items.title: PhD AI/ML Research Engineer Intern
items.desc: Craft: Technology & Development Job Description: AI/ML Research Engineer Internship - 2027 About AI Labs at King’s AI Center of Excellence: Join AI Labs, an applied research team within King’s AI Center of Excellence, where innovation and collaboration come together to tackle complex modeling challenges and explore the latest advances in machine learning. At AI Labs, we help unlock business value through impactful research and the development of state-of-the-art solutions. Our work spans automation at scale for game levels, player experience optimization, AI trustworthiness, and the exploration of emerging technologies. Working alongside Research Engineers, ML Engineers, and Data Scientists, you will contribute to long-term research initiatives and play an important role in advancing King’s central machine learning capabilities. The Opportunity: For this internship cycle, we are looking for a motivated Research Engineer Intern with a strong interest in one of the following research themes: World Models for Gameplay and Simulation: Investigate scalable world models that learn predictive representations and dynamics from gameplay data to support simulation, planning, and downstream decision-making. Familiarity with generative modeling, latent dynamics models, model-based reinforcement learning, and self-supervised learning is desirable. Particular interest will be given to approaches that improve generalization, sample efficiency, and long-horizon prediction. Reinforcement Learning for Gameplay: Apply advanced Reinforcement Learning (RL) techniques to enhance playtesting and support the creation of more engaging player experiences. Candidates with a strong background in RL and hands-on experience with modern online and offline RL algorithms, particularly in transfer learning and robust policy generalization, are encouraged to apply. Experience with unsupervised RL, exploration and intrinsic motivation, or related approaches is highly desirable. Understanding User Behavior in Games: Leverage quantitative and qualitative methods, together with multi-modal data, to deepen our understanding of player strategies, behaviors, and skill progression. Experience combining behavioral analytics with advanced machine learning techniques to identify meaningful patterns in behavioral data will be highly valuable. This is a fixed-term internship of six months , offering the opportunity to work on cutting-edge machine learning research that contributes directly to game content and player experiences. You will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced environment, developing solutions with real-world impact across our products and services. The role is based in our Stockholm office and is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement. Responsibilities: Collaborate with researchers and engineers on projects aligned with your area of interest and expertise. Participate in the full research lifecycle, from problem definition and methodology exploration to implementation, experimentation, and evaluation. Document research outcomes and communicate progress and findings to team members and relevant stakeholders. Who You Are: Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field. Recent graduates with relevant backgrounds are also welcome to apply. Strong foundation in machine learning, data science, and algorithm development. Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. Knowledge of, or prior experience with, the research topic and methodologies relevant to the selected theme is preferred. Proficient in Python and experienced with machine learning libraries and frameworks. Hold valid authorization to work in Sweden from January 2027 onward. How to Apply: To apply for the Research Engineer Intern position at AI Labs within King’s AI Center of Excellence, please submit: 1) your CV, and 2) a cover letter outlining: Your interest in the role. Your preferred research theme. Relevant experience, including links to projects, publications, or other work where applicable. Contact details for your academic supervisor. Please ensure that all application materials are submitted before the application deadline. We look forward to hearing from you. About King With a mission of Making the World Playful, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world with more than 20 years of history of delivering some of the world’s most iconic games in the mobile gaming industry, including the world-famous Candy Crush franchise, as well as other mobile titles such as Farm Heroes Saga. Around 200 million people play a King game every month. King, part of Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), has Kingsters in Stockholm, Malmö, London, Barcelona, Berlin, Dublin, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles and Malta. More information can be found at King.com or by following us on LinkedIn and @lifeatking on Instagram.

items.title: PhD Studentship: Dynamic Performance and AI-Driven Optimisation of Hybrid Energy Systems for Net Zero
items.desc: Area Foundation Eng.& Physical Sciences Location UK Other Closing Date Open Until Filled Reference ENG416 Programme Length: 4 Years Study Mode: Full-time Location: Nottingham Discipline: Engineering & Physical Sciences Start Date: December 2026 Project Overview This fully funded PhD project aims to develop and evaluate a novel hybrid energy system integrating gas turbines, low-temperature carbon capture, biomass gasification, and advanced solar thermal technologies to enable carbon-negative fuel production and grid support. The research will focus on developing intelligent energy systems capable of reducing carbon emissions, improving grid stability, and enhancing sustainable energy generation. The project combines thermodynamic modelling, transient simulation, techno-economic assessment, life cycle analysis, and AI-driven optimisation to support the UK's net-zero ambitions. Research Objectives The successful candidate will: Develop thermodynamic models of integrated hybrid energy systems. Conduct transient simulations using UK climate and grid demand profiles. Evaluate system performance under varying operating conditions. Perform techno-economic and life cycle assessments. Develop AI-driven optimisation and intelligent control strategies. Investigate opportunities for deployment across industrial applications, including steel, cement, and waste-to-energy sectors. Supervisory Team Dr Ioanna Dimitriou, University of Nottingham Dr Oliver Fisher, University of Nottingham About The Net2Zero Centre For Doctoral Training The Net2Zero CDT is a partnership between Aston University, the University of Nottingham, Queen's University Belfast, and the University of Warwick. Students benefit from: Access to world-class research facilities. Collaboration with academic and industrial partners. International networking opportunities. Training in engineering, communication, entrepreneurship, and business skills. A three-month industrial, research, or policy placement. Candidate Profile Applicants should hold, or expect to obtain, a First-Class or strong 2:1 degree (or equivalent) in: Chemical Engineering Mechanical Engineering Energy Engineering Process Engineering Or a closely related discipline A background in thermodynamics, energy systems, process modelling, programming, or simulation tools such as MATLAB, Python, Aspen Plus, TRNSYS, or EES is desirable. items.title: PhD Position in Entrepreneurship, AI, and Labor Market Disruption - DTU Entrepreneurship
items.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
items.desc: Job Description Are you interested in exploring the following questions? How are artificial intelligence (AI) and automation reshaping individuals' transitions to entrepreneurship? How do individuals' skills, experience, and technological readiness influence the types of businesses they create and their subsequent performance? How do these patterns vary across countries and institutional contexts? DTU Entrepreneurship invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship as part of an international research project entitled The New Landscape of Necessity Entrepreneurship: Understanding Entrepreneurial Transitions in an Era of AI- and Automation-Driven Labor Market Disruption . The project investigates how AI and automation reshape entrepreneurial transitions, with particular attention to individuals who start businesses following unemployment. The PhD candidate will join an international research team involving Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Professor Marc Gruber at École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland, and Professor John C. Dencker at Northeastern University, USA. Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF), the project combines large-scale surveys, Danish administrative registry data, and qualitative interviews across Denmark, Switzerland, and Greece. The position offers an opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge entrepreneurship research, work with rich international datasets, and collaborate with leading scholars in the field. Responsibilities And Qualifications Your primary responsibility will be to conduct high-quality research within the international project, with opportunities to develop your own research questions within its overall scope. Your tasks will include: Developing research questions and theoretical frameworks concerning entrepreneurship, human capital, AI, and labor market transitions. Applying quantitative and qualitative research methods to investigate entrepreneurial transitions and outcomes. Collecting, managing, and analyzing quantitative data, including large-scale surveys and Danish registry data. Contributing to the design and implementation of surveys and qualitative interviews in collaboration with international research partners. Preparing research papers for submission to leading international academic journals. Presenting research findings at international conferences and contributing to dissemination activities targeting policymakers and other stakeholders. Collaborating with researchers at DTU, EPFL, Northeastern University, and other project partners. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in entrepreneurship research and technological change. We expect you to have: A Master’s degree. A strong interest in developing quantitative research and analytical skills. Excellent written and spoken English communication skills. The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment. The following qualifications would be considered an advantage, but are not required: Experience working with large-scale datasets, registry data, or longitudinal data. Experience with statistical software such as Stata or R, and familiarity with econometric techniques, including regression analysis and panel data methods. Experience with survey design, qualitative interviewing, or mixed-methods research. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . Assessment The assessment of applicants will be conducted by Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, who will serve as the principal supervisor. We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is as soon as possible or as agreed with the successful candidate. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, DTU Entrepreneurship, Technical University of Denmark, at argnik@dtu.dk . You can read more about DTU Entrepreneurship at www.entrepreneurship.dtu.dk . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 8 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time) . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file . The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. DTU Entrepreneurship is amongst the leading international entities in technology entrepreneurship and helps develop an entrepreneurial culture across DTU. As part of a dynamic and evolving ecosystem, we combine practice-oriented education and research in entrepreneurship with real start-up opportunities from all DTU departments. With rigorous research at its core, the Center builds the entrepreneurial capabilities of students, industry leaders, academics and policymakers to address unsolved problems, and together create new knowledge, methodologies and initiatives. We enable ethically minded entrepreneurs to build solutions that benefit people, society and the world. The Center experiments with new entrepreneurial methodologies and activities to push boundaries within research and education. DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

items.title: PhD Position in Secure and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning / AI (m/f/d)

Our goal is to build a flexible and trustworthy IoT platform based on reliable electronics and secure communication methods. The Trustworthy Data Processing group at the Barkhausen Institut is seeking a highly motivated candidate to pursue a PhD in secure and privacy-preserving machine learning and AI. At the earliest possible date we are looking for a PhD Position in Secure and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning / AI (m/f/d) The position combines academic research with practical system development, including developing new methods, implementing prototypes, and evaluating their security, privacy, and efficiency. The position will initially be filled for a period of 2 years and will be remunerated in line with TV-L E-13. The position aims at supporting further academic qualification (e.g. PhD). Your Responsibilities Will Include Conduct research in secure and privacy-preserving machine learning and AI towards a PhD. Develop and evaluate methods and prototypes and publish research findings. Contribute to collaborative research projects, including preparing project deliverables and reports. Present research findings at conferences, workshops, and project meetings. We expect the following Above-average university degree in the field of our research focus (cryptography, security, privacy) A strong academic background and relevant research experience; Programming experience and an interest in developing research prototypes; An interest in combining scientific research with practical system development. Very good written and spoken English skills We especially welcome applicants with a background in both of the following areas: Privacy-enhancing technologies, such as homomorphic encryption, trusted execution environments, and secure computation; Machine learning and AI You are interested, but you don’t think you meet all the requirements of the job posting? Then you should know: We don’t hire resumes, we hire people. We are looking for potential and want to actively foster it. That’s why we encourage you to apply! If you meet all the professional requirements (diploma/master's degree), this position is classified as TV-L E 13. Depending on your professional experience, the basic monthly salary ranges between €4,629 and €6,580. We will be happy to provide more details during the interview. If you have passion for new technologies and the desire to develop the connected world of tomorrow with us, we are looking for you. Life and science are compatible at our institute. We offer a range of recognised family-friendly measures, such as part-time work, mobile working and flexible working hours that take family needs into account. We also offer support for arriving in Dresden (all formalities, apartment etc.). Application Procedure Your application should include motivation letter including a short statement outlining your research interests and relevant experience, CV, copy of university degree certificate, short summary of Master thesis. Barkhausen Institut strives for gender and diversity equality. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Severely disabled persons are given preference in the event of equal suitability. We only accept complete documents as one single PDF document by e-mail to hier . Please reference “PhD Position in Secure and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning / AI” in the subject line. Applications that contain other file formats (e.g. Word, Excel) will not be considered in the selection process. Informal inquiries can also be submitted to the same address. If you have any content-related questions regarding the job advertisement, you can contact Maryam Zarezadeh at hier . Please apply until October 31, 2026. The data submitted by you in the course of the application procedure will be processed by the Barkhausen Institut (BI). BI shall use the data for the purposes of the application procedure. No data shall be passed on to third parties. items.title: Promovendus klinisch redeneren en AI: leren in een gesimuleerde zorgwereld
items.desc: Fascineert het je hoe artsen leren redeneren? En wil je meebouwen aan de toekomst van medisch onderwijs, met simulatie, virtuele patiënten en AI? Dan nodigen we je uit als promovendus om te onderzoeken hoe we klinisch redeneren kunnen trainen als de 'echte' patiënt niet altijd binnen handbereik is. Aantal uur: 28 • 36 uur per week Werklocatie: Locatie VUmc Contractvorm: Bepaalde tijd Salaris: € 3.217 - € 4.077 Reageer tot en met: 26 oktober 2026 Wat ga je doen? Je exploreert de literatuur op de huidige state-of-the-art rond bovenstaande onderwerpen. Je schrijft een algemeen onderzoeksplan en plannen voor deelstudies met bijbehorende ethische goedkeuringen. Je onderzoekt welke onderdelen van klinisch redeneren (zoals het toepassen van fundamentele kennis, het verzamelen van informatie, het afwegen van diagnoses en het formuleren van beleid) zich lenen voor welke vorm van simulatie, en welke taken juist de echte patiënt vragen. Je onderzoekt hoe AI, zoals LLM-gebaseerde chatbots, kan helpen bij het genereren van realistische casuïstiek op maat, het simuleren van patiënten en het geven van feedback op het redeneerproces, en hoe betrouwbaar en onderwijskundig effectief dat is. Je werkt hierbij samen met docenten en studenten, bijvoorbeeld in het Klinisch Trainingscentrum, de Living Library en de studentenpoli. Samen met onderwijskundigen en docenten in het Amsterdam UMC die al ervaring opdoen met LLM-gebaseerde chatbots in het onderwijs, ontwikkel en evalueer je (pilot)onderwijs voor coassistenten. Je verzamelt en analyseert data uit onder andere experimentele studies, met kwalitatieve en kwantitatieve methoden, en interpreteert de bevindingen in de context van het medisch onderwijs. Je schrijft wetenschappelijke artikelen voor (inter)nationale tijdschriften en brengt de resultaten uiteindelijk samen in jouw proefschrift. Je presenteert jouw bevindingen op nationale en internationale congressen en bouwt zo aan een sterk academisch profiel en netwerk. Je volgt onder andere cursussen vanuit de Doctoral School Amsterdam UMC die aansluiten bij het project en bij jouw eigen ambities, en krijgt de mogelijkheid om ervaring op te doen in het verzorgen van onderwijs en het begeleiden van studenten. Wat neem je mee? Je hebt een afgeronde (research)master in onderwijskunde, cognitieve psychologie, gezondheidswetenschappen, geneeskunde, biomedische wetenschappen, informatiekunde of een vergelijkbaar vakgebied; Je hebt affiniteit met onderzoek. Ervaring met onderzoek waarbij je gebruik hebt gemaakt van kwalitatieve en/of kwantitatieve onderzoeksmethoden is een pré; Interesse in klinisch redeneren, medisch onderwijs, simulatieleren en de rol van AI in de zorg en het onderwijs, en de nieuwsgierigheid om je hier verder in te verdiepen; Je bent analytisch sterk, zelfstandig en kritisch, en je hebt het doorzettingsvermogen om een promotietraject tot een goed einde te brengen; Je kunt complexe materie helder overbrengen; ervaring met onderwijs of begeleiden is een plus; Je bent een teamspeler die zowel zelfstandig als binnen een groot multidisciplinair team (artsen, psychologen, onderwijskundigen en technici) kan werken; Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels uitstekend, zowel schriftelijk als mondeling. Wat bieden we jou? Je treedt in dienst bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. De startdatum is zo snel mogelijk. Een contract voor de duur van 12 maanden, met de intentie te verlengen tot een totaal van vier jaar. Voor deze vacature geldt de Richtlijn Promovendi. Inschaling in salarisschaal OIO: € 3.217 tot € 4.077 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Artsen worden ingeschaald in salarisschaal 10: € 3.724 tot € 5.867 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Daarnaast ontvang je 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering. Bereken hier jouw netto salaris. Vakantie-uren: 194,4 uur per jaar bij een fulltime dienstverband en de mogelijkheid om uren bij te sparen. 100% OV-vergoeding. Kom je lopend, fietsend of met de auto? Dan ontvang je een vergoeding van €0,21 per km (voor de auto geldt een maximum van 40 km enkele reis). Kom je op de fiets? Maak gebruik van onze goede fietsregeling. Pensioenopbouw bij BeFrank, een modern, begrijpelijk en eerlijk geprijsd pensioen. Bekijk deze video met meer informatie over de indiensttreding bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Waar ga je werken ? Je maakt deel uit van het team Onderzoek van Onderwijs binnen de Faculteit Geneeskunde VU. Daarnaast neem je actief deel aan het netwerk i.o. voor onderzoek van onderwijs binnen Amsterdam UMC. Amsterdam UMC Research BV Amsterdam UMC Research BV ondersteunt wetenschappelijk onderzoek zonder winstoogmerk. Hiermee voorzien we onderzoekers in alles wat ze nodig hebben om te kunnen excelleren. Zo bieden onze principal investigators (PI's) en projectleiders begeleiding op het gebied van projectbeheer, finance en human resources. Bij medisch-wetenschappelijke onderzoeksprojecten wordt daarnaast ook ondersteuning op juridisch vlak geboden. Bekijk de video voor meer informatie. Wat ga je onderzoeken? Klinisch redeneren is de kern van het artsenvak: het vermogen om uit het patiëntverhaal, de uitgevraagde klachten, het lichamelijk onderzoek en onderzoeksuitslagen de juiste diagnose en het juiste plan te destilleren. Het is geen losse vaardigheid, maar een samenspel van veel onderdelen: fundamentele (bio)medische kennis, het verzamelen van informatie, het afwegen van diagnoses en het opstellen van beleid. Tijdens de coschappen leren geneeskundestudenten dit door te observeren, te oefenen met medestudenten en simulatiepatiënten, maar bovenal door dit daadwerkelijk uit te voeren bij de patiënt. Maar juist die leeromgeving staat onder druk. Door o.a. hoge werkdruk, fusies van ziekenhuizen, beperkte financiële ruimte, uitplaatsing naar zelfstandige behandelcentra (ZBC’s) en verplaatsing van zorg naar de eerste lijn neemt de opleidingscapaciteit van coassistenten af. Daardoor is het voor coassistenten steeds lastiger om voldoende, gevarieerde en veilige oefenmomenten met echte patiënten te krijgen. Terwijl we juist die momenten nodig hebben om artsen goed op te leiden in klinisch redeneren. Simulatie en virtuele patiënten bieden een veelbelovend alternatief om studenten in de geneeskundeopleiding voor te bereiden op het zelfstandig zien van patiënten: studenten kunnen op hun eigen niveau veilig oefenen met een breed scala aan casuïstiek, zonder risico voor patiënten, en met directe feedback. AI maakt dat nu schaalbaar. Denk aan taalmodellen die realistische patiëntcasuïstiek genereren op maat van de student, die als virtuele patiënt een anamnese kan laten afnemen, of die als tutor kan meedenken en feedback geven op het redeneerproces zelf. Maar belangrijke vragen zijn nog onbeantwoord. Welke onderdelen van klinisch redeneren leer je goed in welke vorm van simulatie (van een virtuele patiënt achter een scherm, een simulatiepatiënt van vlees en bloed, tot een teamsimulatie met acteurs), en welke leer je het best bij een ‘echte’ patiënt? Hoe realistisch en betrouwbaar is de met behulp van AI gegenereerde casuïstiek? En hoe zorgen we dat studenten zowel leren klinisch redeneren mét AI als zélf kritisch blijven redeneren? Daar ga jij als promovendus onderzoek naar doen. Laten we kennismaken Let op: voeg bij je sollicitatie ook jouw publicatielijst mee aan het einde van jouw motivatiebrief of cv (indien relevant). De eerste ronde sollicitatiegesprekken starten in de week van 26 oktober . Deze gesprekken worden gehouden met de vice-decaan onderwijs FdG VU en het hoofd onderzoek van onderwijs FdG VU. Heb je nog vragen? Voor inhoudelijke informatie over deze vacature kun je terecht bij Martine de Bruijne , vice-decaan onderwijs FdG VU, via mc.debruyne@amsterdamumc.nl . Een referentiecheck en screening kunnen onderdeel zijn van de procedure. Kom je bij ons in dienst, dan vragen we voor een aantal functiegroepen standaard een VOG (Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag). Bekijk wat het inhoudt en of het voor jouw functie van toepassing is. Interne kandidaten krijgen, bij gelijke geschiktheid, voorrang op externe kandidaten. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗔𝗡𝗧 𝗙𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗢𝗥𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 This announcement concerns candidate recruitment for a competitive 𝗙𝗣𝗨 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗼𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗳𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽 application. 𝗦𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗯𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵 𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗽 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗴𝘂𝗮𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗲 𝗳𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗻 𝗲𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗼𝘆𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁. Appointment is conditional on a successful funding application and fulfilment of the applicable eligibility and doctoral admission requirements. 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗝𝗘𝗖𝗧 𝗗𝗘𝗦𝗖𝗥𝗜𝗣𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝘊𝘩𝘰𝘰𝘴𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢 𝘴𝘶𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘪𝘯𝘢𝘣𝘭𝘦 𝘮𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘢𝘭 𝘪𝘴 𝘰𝘯𝘭𝘺 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘪𝘳𝘴𝘵 𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘱. Product performance also depends on manufacturing processes, component geometry, environmental impacts and safety requirements. This PhD project aims to develop and validate an 𝗔𝗜-𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗱𝗶𝗴𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺 integrating these factors into evidence-based composite-product design and development. The doctoral researcher will create a 𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗲𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 linking materials, processing conditions and product performance, and develop 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝘀 to identify promising 𝘮𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘢𝘭–𝘱𝘳𝘰𝘤𝘦𝘴𝘴–𝘥𝘦𝘴𝘪𝘨𝘯 combinations. 𝗦𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝗮𝗳𝗲𝘁𝘆-𝗯𝘆-𝗱𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 criteria will support the comparison of alternative solutions. 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 will help users interact with validated computational tools while explicitly identifying uncertainty and evidence limitations. Research activities will combine experimental materials development, composite manufacturing, mechanical testing, physicochemical characterisation, modelling, machine learning, sustainability assessment and technology transfer. items.title: Wissenschaftliche/-r Mitarbeiter/-in (m/w/d) - Promotionsstelle
items.desc: Die Technische Universität Clausthal ist eine forschungsstarke Universität mit hoher nationaler und internationaler Vernetzung. Die rund 80 Professor:innen, 1.100 Beschäftigten sowie 3.000 Studierenden genießen kurze Wege, einen persönlichen Umgang und die faszinierende Landschaft inmitten des UNESCO-Welterbes Harz. Die TU Clausthal ist als größte Arbeitgeberin der Region der wichtigste Wirtschaftsfaktor und bietet kulturelle Vielfalt und Internationalität. Die TU Clausthal hat sich gesamtuniversitär dem Leitthema der „Circular Economy“ verpflichtet und verfolgt das Ziel, in Forschung, Lehre und Verwaltung am Aufbau einer nachhaltigen Gesellschaft im digitalen Zeitalter mitzuwirken. Die Arbeitsgruppe Technische Informatik am Institut für Informatik sucht zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine:einen Wissenschaftliche:r Mitarbeiter:in (m/w/d) - Promotionsstelle im Bereich neuartiger Prozessoren und KI-Beschleuniger Die Stelle ist zunächst auf die Dauer von 3 Jahren befristet (Kennziffer: CE26-1) und mit 100% der regelmäßigen wöchentlichen Arbeitszeit zu besetzen. Die Bereitschaft zur akademischen Qualifikation wird vorausgesetzt. Die Stelle ist grundsätzlich teilzeitgeeignet. Die Arbeitsgruppe Technische Informatik am Institut für Informatik der TU Clausthal forscht im Bereich des modernen Hardware-Entwurfs, mit dem Ziel leistungsfähiger sowie energie- und ressourceneffizienter Rechnersysteme. Einen Schwerpunkt bildet die Prozessorentwicklung, von Erweiterungen der offenen RISC-V-Architektur bis zu neuartigen Prozessorkonzepten. Weitere Themen sind Hardware für neuronale Netze und Approximate Computing. Unsere Forschung umfasst die gesamte Designkette von der Logiksynthese bis zur Implementierung auf FPGAs; dabei nutzen und erweitern wir moderne Hardwarebeschreibungssprachen wie Chisel und Clash. Sie interessieren sich für Rechnerarchitektur und Hardwareentwurf und möchten promovieren? Dann unterstützen Sie die Arbeitsgruppe Technische Informatik in einem der folgenden Themenbereiche: Prozessorentwicklung: Die Arbeitsgruppe forscht an RISC-V Prozessoren und deren Erweiterungen sowie an neuartigen Prozessorarchitekturen, die ohne klassische Register auskommen. Die Aufgaben reichen von der Konzeption bis zur ersten Hardware-Implementierung auf FPGAs. Hardware-Beschleuniger für Spiking Neural Networks: Die Arbeitsgruppe forscht an energieeffizienten Hardware-Beschleunigern für Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) und hat dafür eine eigene Architektur sowie Chisel-basierte Entwurfswerkzeuge entwickelt. Die Aufgaben reichen von der Weiterentwicklung der Architektur und der Werkzeuge bis zur Umsetzung größerer Netze und neuer Anwendungen auf FPGAs. Aufgabengebiet Forschung in einem der beiden Themengebiete mit dem Ziel der Promotion Veröffentlichung Ihrer Ergebnisse auf internationalen Konferenzen und in Fachzeitschriften Mitwirkung in der Lehre im üblichen Umfang, auf Deutsch oder Englisch Einstellungsvoraussetzungen Vorausgesetzt werden: Mit überdurchschnittlichen Noten abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master oder gleichwertig) in Informatik, Elektrotechnik, Computational Engineering oder einer verwandten Fachrichtung Team- und Kommunikationsfähigkeit Bereitschaft zur Kooperation mit nationalen und internationalen Partnern Hohes Engagement und Selbstständigkeit Kenntnisse in Rechnerarchitektur und im Umgang mit FPGAs Gute Englischkenntnisse wünschenswert: Kenntnisse von RISC-V, Chisel, (Spiking) Neural Networks Was wir bieten Die Möglichkeit zur Promotion in einem aktiven Forschungsumfeld, mit viel Freiraum für eigene Ideen und persönlicher Betreuung Eine abwechslungsreiche und anspruchsvolle Tätigkeit in dem lebendigen Umfeld einer Hochschule eine tarifliche Vergütung nach dem Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst der Länder (TV-L), sowie zum Jahresende eine Jahressonderzahlung nach dem TV-L und eine separate Zusatzversorgung als Betriebsrente (VBL), 30 Tage Urlaub sowie arbeitsfreie Tage an Heiligabend und Silvester Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Familie durch flexible Arbeits- und Teilzeitmodelle sowie Mobilem Arbeiten im Rahmen der dienstlichen Möglichkeiten betriebliches Gesundheitsmanagement, Angebote des Hochschulsports sowie über Corporate Benefits zukunftsorientierte Entwicklungs- und Qualifizierungsmöglichkeiten die Möglichkeit zur aktiven Mitwirkung an der Weiterentwicklung unserer Universität alle Vorteile einer Beschäftigung im öffentlichen Dienst Haben wir Ihr Interesse geweckt? Bewerben Sie sich auf unserer Homepage über den Button "Online-Bewerbung" (siehe unten). Gleichstellung mit ihren Facetten, Chancengerechtigkeit, Diversität und Familienfreundlichkeit ist der TU Clausthal ein wichtiges Anliegen. Menschen mit Schwerbehinderung werden bei entsprechender Eignung mit Vorrang berücksichtigt. Die Bewerbungen von Menschen aller Nationalitäten sind willkommen. Wir freuen uns auf Sie! Kontakt: Für fachliche Fragen steht Ihnen Prof. Oliver Keszöcze (oliver.keszoecze@tu-clausthal.de, +49 5323 72-7153) gern zur Verfügung. Ihre Bewerbungsunterlagen reichen Sie bitte in einer PDF-Datei ein. Bewerbungen sind mit den üblichen Unterlagen bis spätestens zum 15.11.2026 über unser Online-Portal (siehe unten) möglich. PhD position: modeling menopause-related heart rhythm disorders
items.desc: Job Description Menopause induces profound electrical and structural changes in the heart, yet the mechanisms driving this transition, and the reasons it dramatically increases the risk of heart rhythm disorders in women, remain largely unexplored. In this PhD project, you will play a central role in uncovering these mechanisms by developing advanced, multi‑scale computational models of atrial electrophysiology. You will work with one of the most comprehensive and unique datasets available worldwide: high‑resolution intra‑operative electrical mapping data recorded directly from the human atria during cardiac surgery, combined with ECG, PPG, hormone profiles, and continuous vital signs. All data is collected within Erasmus MC, giving you direct access to clinicians, engineers, and the surgical team collecting the data. This means you will not rely on synthetic or incomplete datasets but you will build models grounded in rich, real-world physiology. Your task is to transform these multimodal datasets into patient‑specific “digital twins” that simulate how atrial electrophysiology evolves across the menopausal transition. You will design and calibrate mechanistic models at the cellular, tissue, and organ scale; develop numerical methods and optimization pipelines; and run large-scale simulations to reconstruct remodeling trajectories and identify the critical “breaking points” that lead to arrhythmias such as sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation. The mechanistic insights and model outputs you generate will directly feed into the women‑specific arrhythmia detection algorithms developed by our industrial partner. Your work will therefore have a clear translational pathway toward real‑world digital health solutions. Beyond modeling, you will contribute to algorithm development for arrhythmia prediction and collaborate closely with clinical researchers during patient recruitment and data collection. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys combining computational modeling, physiology, and real clinical data. Your work will directly advance women‑specific arrhythmia detection and care, making a scientific impact that is both academically significant and clinically meaningful. “What I enjoy most is seeing how mathematical models can reveal mechanisms that cannot be directly observed from data.” - team member The position will be available by Q4 2026. The project is funded by Health-Holland. Work environment You will conduct your research within the Translational Electrophysiology Unit of the Department of Cardiology at Erasmus MC. The group is internationally recognized for its work on cardiac electrophysiology and collaborates closely with the Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery and multiple research groups at TU Delft. You will join a multidisciplinary, inclusive, and collegial team of clinicians, engineers, and scientists who work together to understand and treat cardiac arrhythmias. The environment is dynamic, supportive, and rich in opportunities for scientific growth. Qualifications And Skills We are looking for a motivated researcher with: A MSc or MEng degree in Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Computational Science, or a related field. Strong interest in computational modeling, simulations, or mathematical physiology. Experience with dynamical systems, numerical simulation, or finite‑element–based modeling approaches is a strong plus. Programming experience (preferably Python, but other languages are also a plus). Affinity with clinical or patient‑related research. Excellent communication skills and ability to work in a multidisciplinary team. Strong analytical mindset and enthusiasm for scientific discovery. Terms of employment A full‑time, 4‑year PhD position. A gross monthly salary between € 3.217,- and € 4.077,- (scale OIO) based on a full-time workweek of 36 hours. A salary increase of 3.5% from May 2027, according to the collective labor agreement (CLA). Excellent fringe benefits, such as a 13th month that is already paid out in November and an individual travel expense package. Pension insurance with ABP. We take care of approximately 2/3 of the monthly contribution. Special benefits, such as an incompany physiotherapist and bicycle repairer. And there is also a gym where you can work on your fitness after work. A supportive team and excellent supervision. Opportunities to attend international conferences and courses. A dynamic research environment at the largest academic medical center in the Netherlands. More information Make this job your next career move! Apply now using the application button. For more information about the role, please contact Dr. Vehpi Yildirim, Department of Cardiology (mail (mailto:v.yildirim@erasmusmc.nl)or +31 (0)6 812 496 74), or Prof. Dr. Natasja de Groot, Department of Cardiology, Erasmus MC via mail (mailto:n.m.s.degroot@erasmusmc.nl).

items.title: Doctoral Researcher, MSCA Doctoral Network position “Electric solar wind sail mission design”
items.desc: MSCA Doctoral Network position “Electric solar wind sail mission design” We are now looking for two (2) Doctoral Researchers. This PhD topic is part of the “Electric solar wind sail doctors” (E-Sailors) network, funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network Programme. The E-Sailors network is designed to train the next generation of Electric solar wind sail (E-sail) scientists, developers and advocates. This particular Doctoral Researcher (DR) will work with in-orbit results of on-going missions, such as Foresail-1 p developed by Aalto University with the E-sail payload from the Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI), as well as the DR will develop new and improved in-orbit E-sail experiments for future missions in lunar orbit and deep space. The DR will be enrolled at and hosted by Aalto University, Finland, with the main supervisor Jaan Praks, co-hosted by the FMI with the E-sail researcher Dr. Petri Toivanen. Research field : Space technology, payload development Supervisor : Jaan Praks Offered by : Aalto University, School of Electrical Engineering General Description Of Programme And Host The Electric solar wind Sail doctors (E-Sailors) is a challenge-based Doctoral Network that aims to bring Electric solar wind sail (E-sail) from low Earth orbit (LEO) demonstration missions to the operational environment of the solar wind. It is delivered by 8 universities in cooperation with FMI, where E-sail was invented, and 4 companies. E-sail is a highly innovative and potentially disruptive propellantless propulsion system. An operational E-sail consists of hair-thin and kilometres-long wires, or tethers, which are charged at a high voltage creating an electrostatic sheath (electric sail) which deflects solar wind particles and generates the propulsive effect in interplanetary environment. Successful and rapid development and deployment of the technology will ensure EU's leadership in the exploration and exploitation of deep space, the next commercial space frontier. The programme is designed to achieve the following training objectives for our doctoral researchers: Equip them with core scientific skills and specialised knowledge in designing experiments for demonstrating space technologies and developing space missions; Provide them with a wide range of transferrable skills, such as Open Science and FAIR, communicating science to public, advocacy, networking etc.; Develop their business and entrepreneurship skills, such as IPR management, preliminary business planning, pitching to investors, starting start-ups. Aalto University is a leading Finnish university combining science, technology, design, and business to foster innovation and multidisciplinary research. The Aalto Space Lab is a comprehensive facility dedicated to the development, integration, and qualification of small satellites and space payloads. The laboratory features an advanced electronics development environment equipped for precision soldering, calibration, functional testing, and sensor characterization. A dedicated cleanroom area supports the assembly and integration of flight hardware, ensuring high reliability and adherence to space standards. Adjacent to the electronics lab, the Space Technology Testing Laboratory provides an advanced thermal–vacuum facility that enables environmental testing of complete satellites and subsystems under simulated space conditions. This includes vacuum, thermal cycling, thermal balance, and outgassing testing, essential for qualifying hardware for launch and orbital operation. The Space Lab also offers access to a wide suite of engineering and simulation software for electronics design, spacecraft systems modelling, structural and thermal analysis, and mission performance verification. Together, these resources support the full development cycle—from early concept design and prototyping to environmental qualification and flight readiness. The Aalto Space Lab serves as a key hub for small satellite and payload research, education, and technology demonstration, supporting academic projects, collaborative research initiatives, and industrial partnerships that advance Finland’s growing role in space technology. Description Of Specific PhD Project Please indicate in your cover letter which of the two positions you are primarily interested in. Position 1: The E-Sailor 8 The E-Sailor 8 doctoral position focuses on developing advanced methods for E-sail tether deployment monitoring and safety, combining simulation, laboratory testing, and in-orbit validation. The candidate will create dynamical and photorealistic 3D models of the tether and spacecraft to support both engineering analysis and visual monitoring during deployment, working in coordination with the RT3D development led by E-Sailor 15. The research includes conducting laboratory and in-orbit experiments using data from the Foresail-1p mission, analysing tether dynamics, imaging, and operational behaviour. Based on these results, the doctoral researcher will propose and evaluate new deployment schemes and safety strategies, contributing to the reliability of future E-sail missions. The work will result in models and validated methods shared with the wider community to support ongoing and upcoming E-sail technology developments. Duration of the work contract and place of employment: The position is based at Aalto University (24 months) with collaboration at CrystalSpace (CS) (12 months), under the supervision of Jaan Praks (Aalto) and Jaan Viru (CS). Position 2: The E-Sailor 4 The E-Sailor 4 doctoral position focuses on the design and engineering of an electric sail (E-sail) payload system for nanospacecraft, with a particular emphasis on developing the payload for the ESTCube-LuNa mission. Building on previous demonstrations such as ESTCube-1, ESTCube-2, and Foresail-1p, the project aims to apply lessons learned to create a more capable and reliable E-sail payload. The work involves analysing previous mission data, defining requirements for new payloads, and designing the mechanical, electrical, and deployment subsystems for ESTCube-LuNa. E-Sailor 4 will also lead the development and testing of a prototype payload, performing functional and environmental tests to verify its performance and requirements for spacecraft integration. The research will result in three main publications covering lessons learned, design development, and prototype testing. In the final project phase, the doctoral researcher will spend 6 months at Spacecraft Anatomy (SA) to gain industrial experience in space hardware manufacturing and qualification. The project will deliver a E-sail payload prototype design and strengthen the technological foundation for future nanospacecraft missions using E-sail propulsion. Duration of the work contract and place of employment: The main supervisor of the DR at Aalto University, Finland (15 months) is Assoc. Prof. Jaan Praks. The DR will also be co-supervised by the E-sail inventor Petri Toivanen while working for 15 months at the FMI, Finland and by Dr. Iaroslav Iakubivskyi while working 6 months at Spacecraft Anatomy, Estonia. Additional details of the positions Starting date: The position is expected to start during 2026. Trial period: 6 months Target degree: Doctoral degree from Aalto University, Finland Approximate gross salary: The salary for a Doctoral Researcher at Aalto University is 3143 EUR per month, which will be adjusted according to the eligible allowances based on MSCA funding. The family allowance will be clarified with the selected candidate once their situation is defined. The salary at FMI is 2900-3200 EUR/month at the beginning of employment. The starting salary at Spacecraft Anatomy is approx. 2700 EUR/month, plus family allowance, if applicable. Requirements For PhD Position Master's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Space Technology, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or closely related field. Excellent command of written and spoken English. Research experience and independent work experience evident through technical projects, theses, publications, or technical reports. This includes the evidence of innovative thinking or novel approaches to technical problems, the ability to synthesize information from multiple sources to advance understanding and demonstrated curiosity and persistence in pursuing technical challenges. Strong academic and development track record with demonstrated proficiency in orbital mechanics and propagators (GMAT, STK, or similar), propulsion systems, spacecraft dynamics, space systems, space mission and environment analyses, cubesats, small spacecraft systems, space plasma physics, software development and version control (Git), simulation software development (experience in multiple fields are considered beneficial). Familiarity with simulation software and numerical methods and proficiency in programming languages (Rust, Python, MATLAB, C/C++, or similar) for simulation and data analysis. Experience in managing multiple concurrent tasks and priorities independently and track record of meeting project deadlines and delivering results without constant supervision. Proven ability to work autonomously on complex technical problems and demonstrated problem-solving skills in technical/engineering contexts. Leadership experience in terms of leading or significantly contributing to multi-month technical projects and taking initiative in research or development activities. Experience working with interdisciplinary and international teams while maintaining individual accountability, such as driving projects forward without extensive guidance. Example of at least one practical project completed within the deadline with minimal supervision, and evidence of self-motivation and proactive problem-solving. Please submit description of personal contributions and level of independence, project outcomes and impact, and references in terms of publications, theses, technical reports, simulations, analysis, code samples, or documentation (multiple references are considered beneficial). The above duties are not exhaustive; the PhD candidate may be required to undertake other tasks consistent with the role and the objectives of the E-Sailors Doctoral Network. Duties And Responsibilities Position 1: The E-Sailor 8 Undertake innovative and independent research on E-sail tether deployment monitoring, dynamics, and safety to enhance the reliability of future nanosatellite missions. Carry out literature reviews, requirement analyses, and theoretical studies on tether mechanics, deployment systems, and in-orbit monitoring approaches. Develop and validate numerical models of tether and spacecraft dynamics, and create photorealistic 3D visualizations to support monitoring and analysis of deployment behaviour. Adapt, develop, and learn new simulation, modelling, and imaging tools, including integration with real-time visualization frameworks such as RT3D. Plan and execute laboratory experiments to characterize tether deployment and verify model performance under controlled conditions. Contribute to in-orbit testing and data analysis activities related to the Foresail-1p mission, including image-based monitoring and interpretation of tether behaviour. Design and propose improved E-sail tether deployment schemes, safety mechanisms, and operational procedures for future missions. Document and communicate research progress through high-quality technical reports, scientific publications, and conference presentations. Collaborate closely with academic and industrial partners at Aalto University and CrystalSpace, while maintaining the ability to work independently and solve technical challenges proactively. Stay up to date with advances in spacecraft dynamics, tether technologies, and on-board imaging systems, integrating new insights into the research. items.title: PhD Position Video-based Hand Motion-tracking for Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis at TU Delft
items.desc: Are you passionate about human movement and developing clinical tools for understanding human movement disorders? Job Description Challenge: Over a quarter of a million people in the Netherlands alone have rheumatoid arthritis (RA) with a majority suffering from debilitating pain and inflammation that makes hand dexterity and work, at times, impossible. While anti-inflammatory and analgesic drugs are the main line of relief, new drugs and treatments are needed and being developed for long-term care. At the same time a major challenge in RA management is quantifying the effectiveness of treatments under real-world conditions. Change: We need technologies to measure and quantify changes in hand function due to daily life factors (sleep, stress, etc.…) and treatments/drugs in the home setting. These technologies would enable drug developers, physiotherapists and physicians to make objective and quantitative assessments regarding the effectiveness of treatments. Impact: Once we understand the effects of stressors and treatments on RA flare ups and hand function, clinicians will be able to more closely target treatments and plan daily routines that minimize pain and suffering from rheumatoid arthritis. We are seeking a PhD candidate for a 4-year contract to develop and apply computational models and video-based tools to capture hand movement and function with deployment in the home environment as the target. Furthermore, you will apply these tools to help us investigate the potential causes and timings of flare ups during patients’ daily lives. You will work primarily with video data, musculoskeletal models, and pose estimation algorithms. The models and algorithms you develop will be part of open source and data repositories affiliated with the broader research program and TU Delft’s commitment to Open Science. You will be an integral part of the ‘Care is coming home!’ program: a 5-year project executed by a large consortium consisting of 2 technical universities (TU Delft, UTwente), 6 hospitals (Amsterdam UMC, Erasmus MC, Leiden UMC, Maartenskliniek, Maastricht UMC, Radboud UMC), 13 companies (Able Human Motion, Biomex, Cue2Walk, DanuSports, Kinetic Analysis, Lode Holding, Madglove, ModelHealth, Moveshelf, Orikami, Sabender (Enterprising Company), Trinoma, VicarVision), 1 rehabilitation centre (Daan Theeuwes Centrum) and 5 patient organisations (Hersenletsel.nl, Hersenstichting, Parkinson Vereniging, ParkinsonNL, ReumaNederland). In total the program will encompass 9 PhDs and 5 postdocs to address the issue of translating health care to the home environment. This PhD position is hosted by the Biomechanical Engineering Department at TU Delft where you will be a part of both the Computational Biomechanics (Seth) and Neuromuscular Control (Mugge) Labs. In addition to research, there are many opportunities to develop your academic career by mentoring and teaching BSc/MSc students, presenting at international conferences, and participating in workshops/training and exchange programs abroad. Job requirements You Should Have MSc in engineering or similar discipline by the start date of the position Experience with mechanical modeling and simulation Experience in computer programming/scripting (e.g., C++, Python, Matlab, etc.) Experience collecting human experimental data (movement, video, or similar) Excellent written and oral communication skills in English The following aspects will help you stand out: Thriving in multidisciplinary environments Curiosity-driven and self-motivated working attitude Knowledge of biomechanical modeling, anatomy, vision-based motion capture, machine learning, control systems Keep in mind that this describes the background we imagine would best fit the role. If you do not meet all the requirements, but believe that you are up for the task, we absolutely want to hear your motivation and how you would fit! The PhD process is a learning experience, so let us know what you want to learn and develop as a PhD candidate. You can view the full job vacancy here. Application deadline: 21 October 2026
